section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren active, what must a driver do immediately?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop.,b:Slow down and stay in lane.,c:Pull to the right and turn on four-way flashers.,d:Drive to the left shoulder and stop
note: You must promptly pull to the right and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement best describes drivers who have consumed alcohol and then drive?
options: a:They do not have sufficient control over their bodies, minds, or vehicles,b:They are always aware of the risks, c:They become better drivers because they are more careful
note: Alcohol is a depressant that reduces judgment, vision, coordination, and reaction time, impairing a driver’s ability to operate a vehicle safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should you do?
options: a:Look and listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,b:Speed up to cross before a train appears.,c:Drive around lowered gates if a car is stuck on the tracks.,d:Keep radio volume high to hear signals better.
note: Always look, listen, and be ready to stop at tracks; do not go around gates or take risks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must a driver respond to a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and continue without stopping.,c:Merge to the right.
note: A flashing red light means stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you socialize and drink alcohol, what is a safe option to ensure safe travel?
options: a:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,b:Drink coffee before driving.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.,d:Wait 10 minutes and then drive
note: Arranging a sober ride home prevents impaired driving; coffee or a shower does not reduce blood alcohol content.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does talking or texting on a cell phone significantly increase crash risk?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Using a handheld or hands-free phone for talking or texting distracts you and increases the likelihood of a crash; it reduces attention and reaction time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?
options: a:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles,b:The decreased stopping distance of trucks,c:The reduced noise levels from larger vehicles
note: Large vehicles need more distance to stop; smaller vehicles should avoid lingering in truck blind spots and give them extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which behavior describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Daydreaming or staring at objects off the roadway while driving.,b:Checking mirrors frequently and scanning traffic.,c:Watching only the car directly ahead.,d:Using turn signals when changing lanes.
note: Inattentive drivers are distracted by non-driving activities and do not adequately scan the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making an emergency roadside stop, is it unnecessary to set the parking brake?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When you make an emergency stop, set your parking brake and turn on your emergency flashers to alert other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal situation requires you to come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed when clear?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A steady yellow light
note: A flashing red light functions like a stop sign: stop, yield to others, and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams, where should you glance?
options: a:Toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Directly at the source of the light.,c:Toward the left side of the road.,d:At the center line for reference.
note: Glance to the right side of the road to avoid temporary blindness from glare while maintaining roadway position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit in business, residential, and school districts unless otherwise posted?
options: a:25 mph,b:15 mph,c:30 mph
note: Unless signs indicate otherwise, the speed limit for passenger vehicles and motorcycles in business, residential, or school areas is 25 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left at an intersection, what is important to do?
options: a:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians,b:Sound your horn to warn oncoming traffic,c:Swing to the right side of your lane to make room
note: Before making a left turn you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians; do not turn unless the way is clear and it is legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What type of signs are typically orange?
options: a:Work zone and construction signs.,b:Regulatory signs like speed limits.,c:School zone signs.,d:Recreational area signs.
note: Orange signs warn of work zones or construction and alert drivers to changing conditions ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' sign mean?
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at this sign.,b:The reduced speed begins at the next sign.,c:You have plenty of time to slow down before the zone.,d:The advisory speed begins after the sign
note: A posted reduced speed sign indicates the new posted speed limit begins at that sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a school crossing sign, what should drivers do?
options: a:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.,b:Always stop even if no children are present.,c:Always sound your horn when children are near.,d:Drive at normal speed if no crossing guard is present
note: Always yield to pedestrians and be alert for children who may enter the crosswalk or roadway unexpectedly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb required?
options: a:Only if other traffic is present,b:Yes — it is required by law and a good habit,c:Only during the maneuver itself
note: You must signal your intentions in advance (Virginia requires signaling at least 100 feet before changing lanes or turning) so other road users can anticipate your actions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you adjust first when you sit in a vehicle before driving?
options: a:Your seat.,b:Your rearview mirror.,c:Your seat belt.
note: Adjust your seat first so you can reach the controls and see the road, then set mirrors and fasten your seat belt.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signs that warn drivers about hazardous conditions are called what?
options: a:Warning signs,b:Regulatory signs,c:Information signs
note: Warning signs (usually yellow with black symbols) advise drivers of potentially hazardous conditions ahead and should be obeyed for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is correct?
options: a:Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.,b:Speeding is safe if you are skilled.,c:Speed has no effect on crash severity.,d:Speeding never results in fatalities
note: Both driving too fast and driving much slower than traffic can be dangerous; speed increases crash severity and risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:When changing lanes,b:When turning left or right,c:When pulling toward or away from a curb,d:All of the above
note: Check blind spots any time you intend to change the vehicle's position—turning, changing lanes, or parking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the safest way to pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much lateral space as possible.,b:Honk to warn them you're passing closely.,c:Drive in the bike lane to get around them.,d:Pass very quickly with no additional clearance.
note: Give bicyclists ample space when passing; do not crowd them and avoid passing too quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals stop working, how should you indicate a turn?
options: a:Use hand signals,b:Use your horn,c:Flash your headlights,d:Use your hazard lights
note: If turn signals fail, use standard hand signals to indicate turns or lane changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection.,d:Traffic signal is malfunctioning and should be ignored.
note: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to slow and proceed carefully through the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:
options: a:Signal, slow gradually, check rearview and watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Speed up and turn sharply.,c:Turn from any lane available without signaling.,d:Rely solely on the horn to warn others.
note: Signal in advance, reduce speed progressively, and yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is NOT a main factor in determining how far it takes to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Steering ability.,b:Perception and reaction distances.,c:Braking distance.,d:Vehicle speed and road conditions.
note: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance — steering skill is not a primary factor.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What helps a person overcome the influence of alcoholic drinks?
options: a:Only the passage of time,b:Hot coffee,c:Fresh air,d:Tomato juice and lime
note: Nothing speeds sobering except time—coffee, fresh air, and other remedies do not eliminate alcohol impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Traffic in the indicated lane must turn in the direction shown and has a protected movement.,b:It only applies on one-way streets.,c:You may go only if a circular green is also lit.,d:You must yield to pedestrians before turning
note: A green arrow gives the same general authority as a circular green but requires traffic in the indicated lane to turn in the arrow's direction, usually with protected right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What can occur if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine,b:The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol,c:The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold
note: Alcohol and many medications interact, often increasing impairment and the risk of dangerous side effects; combining them can multiply their effects.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How does distraction typically affect a driver's reaction to hazards?
options: a:Makes drivers react more slowly,b:Makes drivers react more quickly,c:Has no effect,d:Improves lane-keeping
note: Distracted drivers react more slowly and are more likely to miss hazards, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass on the right of another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead is waiting to turn left and there is a safe available lane to pass,b:Even if it requires driving off the pavement,c:On a narrow bridge,d:Only when signposted
note: You may pass on the right if the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a safe, available lane; you may not leave the paved roadway to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Do pedestrians always have the right-of-way in crosswalks and intersections?
options: a:Yes when they are crossing at intersections—TRUE,b:No—FALSE,c:Only in marked crosswalks,d:Only when traffic lights say so
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when crossing at intersections; crosswalks exist at intersections whether marked or not.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is true about vehicle tires on a wet roadway?
options: a:Higher speeds reduce tire effectiveness and can cause hydroplaning,b:Cars with good tires are unaffected by water,c:Deep water is safer than shallow water,d:Worn tires improve grip on water
note: As speed increases on wet roads, tires lose contact and may hydroplane. Slow down and avoid sudden maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red traffic signal light means you must:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection,b:Stop at the stop line,c:Stop before entering any crosswalk
note: A red signal requires stopping before entering the intersection, at any stop line, and before entering a crosswalk; do not proceed until the light turns green and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the most common color used for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Green.,c:Red.
note: Most warning signs are yellow with black markings and are diamond-shaped to alert drivers of unexpected conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Check your rearview and side mirrors and look over your shoulder to check the blind spot,b:Turn on your headlights,c:Sound your horn to warn other drivers
note: Prior to changing lanes, check mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder to ensure your blind spot is clear before making the lane change.

question: Why must you exercise increased caution when driving at night?
options: a:Vehicles move faster at night,b:Drivers cannot see as well at night,c:Traffic volume is always greater at night
note: At night, visibility is reduced and it is harder to see pedestrians, animals, and hazards. Because you cannot see as far or as clearly, you must use your headlights during hours of darkness and drive more slowly and carefully.

question: If your wheels slip off the pavement edge while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Jerk the wheel to force the vehicle back immediately.,b:Accelerate to get back on quickly,c:Slam on the brakes and stop immediately.,d:Slow down
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, keep a firm grip on the wheel, and slow down gradually. Once you have reduced speed and the car is under control, gently steer back onto the pavement; avoid jerking the wheel or slamming on the brakes.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your blood it tends to:
options: a:Improve your coordination.,b:Slow your reactions and increase errors while driving.,c:Speed up your thinking processes.,d:Make you less confident about driving.
note: As alcohol builds up in your bloodstream, it slows your reaction time, reduces coordination, and impairs judgment. This makes it easier to make driving errors and harder to respond quickly to hazards.

question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:
options: a:Cross quickly whenever you see a train.,b:Look and listen for trains in both directions and only cross when it is safe.,c:Look both ways only when lights are flashing.
note: At railroad crossings, you must both look and listen for trains in both directions, and only cross when you are sure it is safe and clear. Never rely only on warning lights or gates; some crossings may not have active signals, and trains can be very quiet. If a train is approaching, stop and wait until it has passed and the tracks are completely clear before proceeding.

question: Who receives vertical-format driver licenses in Virginia?
options: a:All drivers regardless of age.,b:Persons over age 21.,c:Persons under age 21.,d:Only commercial drivers
note: In Virginia, driver licenses and ID cards issued to persons under age 21 are printed vertically. This vertical format makes it easy for law enforcement and businesses to quickly identify that the holder is under the legal drinking age. Licenses for drivers 21 and older are printed horizontally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and wait for traffic to clear before turning around.,b:Continue to the next exit and safely turn around.,c:Make a U-turn in the travel lane immediately.,d:Back up on the shoulder to reach the missed exit.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, stay calm and continue driving to the next exit. Get off the freeway there, then safely turn around or follow signs to return. Never stop in a travel lane, back up on the shoulder, or make a U‑turn on the freeway, as these actions are extremely dangerous and illegal in most situations.

question: What effect does drinking coffee have on blood alcohol concentration after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Decreases blood alcohol concentration.,b:Cancels the effect of the alcohol.,c:Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
note: Drinking coffee does not lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC). Only time allows your body to metabolize alcohol and reduce BAC. Coffee might make you feel more awake, but you are still impaired and unsafe to drive until enough time has passed for the alcohol to leave your system.

question: What does an 'End school zone' sign indicate?
options: a:The start of a 20 mph zone.,b:The end of a reduced speed school zone.,c:A school crossing ahead,d:That pedestrians are present more often.
note: An 'End school zone' sign tells drivers that the special reduced speed limit for the school zone is over and the regular posted speed limit now applies. You should still stay alert for children and pedestrians, but you are no longer required to follow the school zone’s reduced speed.

question: Which combination provides the most effective protection in a crash?
options: a:Both lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.,b:Lap belt alone.,c:Airbag alone.,d:No restraint is necessary at low speeds.
note: Using both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag together gives you the best protection in a crash. The belt keeps you properly positioned and prevents you from being thrown forward, while the airbag provides extra cushioning in moderate to severe frontal crashes. Airbags are designed to work with seat belts, not replace them.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect driving?
options: a:It is a distracting activity.,b:It helps maintain alertness.,c:It does not affect driving ability.,d:It improves reaction time
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction because it takes at least one hand off the wheel and often your eyes off the road to find, light, or handle the cigarette. Any activity that diverts your attention, hands, or eyes from driving increases your risk of a crash.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:To keep the front wheels straight.,c:In the opposite direction of the skid.,d:Turn the wheel all the way in either direction.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, you should look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This is often described as steering in the direction of the skid, but the key idea is to gently steer toward your intended path, not fight the skid with sudden or opposite steering. Then, as the vehicle regains traction, make small corrections to keep control.

question: Which conviction can result in revocation or suspension of your driver license?
options: a:Driving with snow on your car.,b:Parking in a handicap spot without a placard,c:Failing to stop for a stop sign once.,d:Operating a vehicle under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
note: Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs is a serious offense that can lead to suspension or revocation of your driver license in every state. DUI laws are strict because impairment greatly increases crash risk and the chance of serious injury or death.

question: If involved in an accident, which action should a driver take immediately?
options: a:Leave the scene if no one appears hurt.,b:Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.,c:Always stand in the traffic lanes.,d:Drive home first and report the crash later.
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop at or as close to the scene as possible without blocking traffic more than necessary. Then check for injuries, call emergency services if needed, and exchange information. If the vehicles can be moved safely, move them out of traffic lanes to reduce the risk of another collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When turning left into a driveway.,b:When the car in front of you is disabled.,c:When doing so would interfere with traffic.
note: A single broken line (white between lanes in the same direction, yellow between opposite directions) may be crossed to pass or change lanes only when it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic. If crossing the line would force other drivers to slow, swerve, or brake suddenly, you must not cross.

question: Are most work zone signs orange?
options: a:They are always brown.,b:False — they are usually green.,c:True — work zone signs are typically orange.,d:Only temporary signs are orange.
note: In the U.S., work zone and construction signs are typically orange with black symbols or lettering. They are used to alert drivers to road work, lane closures, and changing traffic patterns so drivers can slow down and proceed with extra caution.

question: Where are roads most likely to freeze quickly in cold or wet weather?
options: a:In the sun.,b:On flat open stretches.,c:On bridges and overpasses.,d:In shaded areas under trees or buildings.
note: Roads tend to freeze first and thaw last in places that are colder than the surrounding pavement. Bridges and overpasses freeze especially quickly because cold air circulates above and below the surface. Shaded areas under trees or buildings also stay colder and can remain icy longer. Use extra caution and reduce speed on bridges, overpasses, and shaded sections in cold or wet weather.

question: On long trips, what helps prevent drowsiness?
options: a:Driving faster than traffic,b:Stopping at regular intervals to rest,c:Opening windows only,d:Turning on the radio loud
note: On long trips, schedule regular stops to get out, walk, stretch, and rest. Short breaks help you stay alert and reduce the risk of drowsy driving. Speeding, loud music, or just opening windows do not safely prevent fatigue and can give a false sense of alertness.

question: What should a small vehicle driver anticipate when passing a large truck?
options: a:Loud music coming from the truck.,b:The truck will always slow down to let you pass.,c:No change in driving behavior is needed.,d:Wind gusts that can affect vehicle stability.
note: When passing a large truck or bus, expect strong wind gusts and air turbulence that can push or pull your vehicle sideways. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, avoid lingering in the truck’s blind spots, and pass promptly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the correct lane, you should:
options: a:Turn from your current lane after signaling.,b:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.
note: If you are not in the correct lane to make a turn, you should not turn from your current lane or cut across traffic at the last moment. Instead, continue straight, go to the next intersection, and make your turn from the proper lane when it is safe.

question: If a driver behind you is driving aggressively, what is the recommended response?
options: a:Stare at the driver as they pass,b:Speed up as they approach,c:Try to get out of the aggressive driver’s way
note: When another driver is aggressive, do not speed up, block them, or stare at them. Safely move out of their way, avoid eye contact, and do not respond to their behavior so the situation does not escalate.

question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:You must always stop before crossing it,b:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,c:Drivers may not pass.,d:Both lanes travel in the same direction.
note: A single dashed yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. You may pass another vehicle when it is safe, there is enough clear distance ahead, and no signs or conditions prohibit passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection controlled by a flashing red signal, what must you do?
options: a:Stop only if other cars are also approaching.,b:Slow down and drive carefully through without stopping.,c:Stop fully, then proceed when it is safe to do so.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question: If an approaching train is close enough to be dangerous, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Flash your lights to warn the train,c:Cross the tracks quickly before the train arrives.,d:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
note: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be a danger, you must not cross the tracks. Wait until the train has completely passed and you have clear visibility in both directions before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:You must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding,b:You must slow down and prepare to stop,c:You may drive through the intersection if it is clear
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, but only if the intersection is clear. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to oncoming traffic when turning left.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstance may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass another car on a hill.,b:Never under any circumstances.,c:To turn into or out of a driveway or make a permitted left turn.,d:To pass a slow-moving car anytime.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing, but you may carefully cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, side road, or to make another permitted left turn when it is safe.

question: Are cell phones a serious source of driver distraction?
options: a:False — they do not affect driving.,b:Only when used for texting.,c:Only for inexperienced drivers.,d:True — they are a serious distraction.
note: Cell phones are a major distraction because they take your eyes, mind, and sometimes hands away from driving. Even hands‑free use can reduce your attention, so limit use to true emergencies.

question: Compared with daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:Always safer,b:No more or less dangerous.,c:Less dangerous.,d:More dangerous.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous because you can see less, it is harder to judge distance and speed, glare from lights can blind you, and there are more tired or impaired drivers on the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:It is never used as a traffic signal,b:It means you may turn in the arrow's direction,c:It has the same meaning as a circular red light — do not proceed
note: A solid red arrow means stop and do not go in the direction of the arrow until it turns green or is replaced by a signal that allows movement. It functions like a red light specifically for that turn.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Only on weekends,b:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.,d:Always
note: Drivers must always be prepared to yield to pedestrians, especially in crosswalks and at intersections. You must stop for pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks and when they are legally crossing the road. Even if a pedestrian is acting unsafely, you should slow or stop if needed to avoid hitting them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must drivers entering an interstate from an entrance ramp do?
options: a:Yield to traffic already on the highway.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Force their way into traffic.,d:Always drive at the posted ramp speed
note: Drivers using an entrance ramp must adjust speed on the ramp and yield to traffic already on the interstate. Do not stop at the end of the ramp unless absolutely necessary; instead, look for a safe gap, signal, and merge smoothly without forcing other vehicles to brake hard or change lanes suddenly.

question: What may happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects are canceled out,b:The effects of both may be increased,c:Nothing will happen,d:It makes you less impaired
note: When alcohol is combined with many prescription, over‑the‑counter, or illegal drugs, the depressant or impairing effects are often multiplied. This can greatly reduce coordination, judgment, and reaction time, making driving far more dangerous than using either substance alone.

question: What can drowsy drivers appear to be doing?
options: a:Being extremely alert,b:Driving defensively,c:Perfectly following the flow of traffic,d:Driving in a manner similar to drunk drivers
note: Drowsy drivers may drift between lanes, react slowly, miss traffic signals, or fail to notice hazards, which can look very similar to the behavior of a drunk driver. Fatigue affects judgment, attention, and reaction time, making it extremely dangerous to drive when you are very tired.

question: In what ways can alcohol affect you while driving?
options: a:It has no effect if you are well rested.,b:It slows reaction time,c:It only affects drivers with little experience.,d:It always improves concentration.
note: Alcohol slows your reaction time, blurs vision, affects balance and coordination, and weakens judgment. Even small amounts can make it harder to respond quickly to hazards, stay in your lane, and make safe decisions, regardless of how rested or experienced you are.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what should you assume?
options: a:Speed up to get past quickly,b:Assume the driver may open the door as you approach,c:Slam on your brakes
note: When passing parked vehicles, you should always assume that a door could open or a person could step out unexpectedly. Slow slightly if needed, leave extra space, and be prepared to brake smoothly so you can avoid a sudden collision with an opening door.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You have a green light and want to turn left but oncoming traffic is heavy. What should you do?
options: a:Use the next intersection to turn,b:Stop at the crosswalk and wait for traffic to clear,c:Wait in the center of the intersection until the oncoming traffic clears
note: With a green light but heavy oncoming traffic, you must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians. It is proper to move into the intersection, keep your wheels straight, and wait there until you have a safe gap. When the traffic clears or the light turns yellow/red, you complete the left turn if it is safe.

question: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and carefully steer back onto the pavement.,b:Stop your car on the edge of the road.,c:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and avoid hard braking or jerking the wheel. Slow down gradually, then gently steer back onto the pavement when your speed is under control and the lane is clear.

question: On slippery roads, what is the safest action to take?
options: a:Speed up to get through the area faster,b:Increase following distance,c:Maintain the posted speed limit but be cautious,d:Reduce your speed
note: On slippery roads from rain, snow, or ice, you must reduce your speed below the posted limit if needed. Slower speeds give your tires more chance to grip and give you more time to react, helping prevent skids and loss of control.

question: If someone drives much slower than the speed limit and blocks traffic, what should they do?
options: a:Always maintain their slow speed regardless of traffic.,b:Drive in the center of the lane to discourage passing,c:Refuse to allow others to pass by speeding up.,d:Pull off the road and let vehicles pass when traffic is backing up.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can be dangerous because it causes others to brake and change lanes suddenly. If your slow speed is causing a line of vehicles to back up, you should safely pull off the road or into a turnout area and let the faster traffic pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What general rule should you follow regarding passing other vehicles?
options: a:Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic at all costs,b:Pass on the right whenever possible,c:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed
note: Passing always carries extra risk because it usually requires moving into another lane and sometimes into oncoming traffic. The safest approach is to drive with the general flow of traffic, stay within the speed limit, and only pass when it is clearly necessary and you have enough space and visibility to do so.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out, what should you do first?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually slow to a stop.,b:Steer sharply to the shoulder at once.,c:Slam on the brakes and stop immediately.,d:Speed up to reach a safe area quickly.
note: When a tire blows out, the car may pull to one side. Grip the steering wheel firmly to keep control, stay off the brakes, and gently ease off the accelerator. Let the vehicle slow down gradually, then signal and steer smoothly to a safe place off the road before stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:Yield to drivers already on the public road.,b:Force their way into traffic.,c:Always have the right-of-way.
note: Drivers entering a public road from a driveway, alley, or private road must yield to all traffic already on the public roadway, including vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians. Enter only when there is a large enough gap so you do not force other road users to slow or change lanes suddenly.

question: A person carrying a white cane or using a guide dog is most likely:
options: a:A blind person.,b:A deaf person.,c:Part of a traffic study.
note: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is usually blind or visually impaired. Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to these pedestrians, stop well back from crosswalks, and never honk or try to hurry them across.

question: How should you respond when approaching road construction or maintenance areas?
options: a:Speed up to get through quickly,b:Be alert for flashing arrow panels and obey all work-zone signs, signals, and flaggers,c:Drive in the middle of the lane and ignore speeds.,d:Pass other vehicles in the work zone.
note: Work zones require extra caution. Slow down to the posted work-zone speed, stay centered in your lane, and be prepared to stop or change lanes. Watch carefully for flashing arrow panels, message boards, signs, cones, and flaggers, and follow their directions. Never speed, weave, or pass other vehicles within the work zone unless directed.

question: Does a double solid yellow line allow passing from either direction?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A double solid yellow line means traffic in both directions is prohibited from crossing the centerline to pass. You must stay in your lane and may only cross when making a permitted left turn into or out of a driveway or side road, if allowed by local law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:Over your right shoulder,b:Over your left shoulder,c:At your side mirror only
note: Before changing lanes, you must check the blind spot by quickly looking over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move. For a left lane change, glance over your left shoulder to see areas not visible in your mirrors.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light instruct drivers to do?
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:Stop completely.,c:Merge only to the right.,d:Yield to all traffic
note: A flashing yellow traffic light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down and proceed with caution, being prepared to yield if necessary to other vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: A court may suspend or revoke your driving privileges for which offense?
options: a:Reckless or aggressive driving (or other serious driving violations).,b:Driving with a valid license.,c:Properly registering your vehicle.,d:Always paying for gasoline.
note: Courts can suspend or revoke your driving privileges for serious traffic offenses such as reckless or aggressive driving, DUI, or repeated major violations. These actions are taken to protect public safety when a driver shows dangerous behavior on the road.

question: What defines your vehicle's blind spot?
options: a:What you see in your rearview mirror.,b:The area illuminated by headlights,c:Areas you cannot see without moving your head.,d:The area directly behind your vehicle.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors and require turning your head to check. They are typically along the sides and slightly behind your vehicle, where another vehicle, bicycle, or motorcycle can be hidden from your mirror view.

question: When approaching a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog or cane, must you yield?
options: a:Only at marked intersections,b:Only if they are in a crosswalk,c:Yes—TRUE,d:No—FALSE
note: Drivers must always yield to blind or visually impaired pedestrians using a white cane or a guide dog, whether or not they are in a marked crosswalk. These pedestrians may need extra time and space to cross safely, and the law gives them clear right‑of‑way to protect them.

question: How do worn or bald tires affect driving?
options: a:They decrease braking distance,b:They have no effect on handling.,c:They can increase stopping distance and make turning more difficult.,d:They improve fuel economy.
note: Worn or bald tires have less tread, which greatly reduces traction. This increases your stopping distance, especially on wet roads, and makes it harder to turn or control the vehicle. Good tread helps channel water away and grip the road; without it, you are more likely to skid or hydroplane.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety step should you take?
options: a:Buckle only backseat passengers.,b:Buckle only child passengers.,c:Ensure you and all passengers have buckled safety belts.,d:Fasten your own seat belt and confirm all passengers are properly restrained.
note: Before starting the engine, you should make sure that you and every passenger are properly buckled. The driver is responsible for checking that all occupants use seat belts or appropriate child restraints, because unbelted passengers can be seriously injured and can also injure others in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow traffic signal indicates that which light will appear next?
options: a:Steady green.,b:Flashing yellow.,c:Steady red.,d:Flashing red
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. It warns you to slow down and stop if you can do so safely before entering the intersection. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, proceed with caution through the intersection before the red appears.

question: May vehicles without special disability plates or placards use designated disabled parking spaces?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Disabled parking spaces are reserved for people with disabilities who have the proper license plates or placards. Parking in these spaces without the required permit is illegal and can result in fines, because it blocks access for those who genuinely need the closer, more accessible parking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when entering a street from a driveway?
options: a:Honk to warn pedestrians.,b:Drive slowly and expect them to yield.,c:Enter as quickly as possible to avoid delaying traffic,d:Stop before entering and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
note: When entering a street from a driveway, you must stop before crossing the sidewalk and the edge of the roadway, check carefully for pedestrians and approaching vehicles, yield to them, and only proceed when it is completely safe.

question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to which road users?
options: a:Both vehicles and pedestrians in and at the entrances to the roundabout,b:Only emergency vehicles,c:Bicyclists and pedestrians within the roundabout,d:Vehicles already in the roundabout
note: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to all traffic already in the circle, including vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians in crosswalks at the entry and exit. Enter only when there is a safe gap so you do not force others to slow or stop suddenly.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn wheels to the right immediately.,b:Pull up even with the car in front of the parking space.,c:Back straight into the space without aligning,d:Turn wheels to the left before positioning.
note: For standard parallel parking, after you signal and confirm the space is safe, you first pull up so your vehicle is parallel and even with the car in front of the space. From that position you then turn your wheels and begin backing into the space.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:
options: a:Drive faster than the train to beat it across the tracks.,b:Look for a way around lowered gates.,c:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching train tracks and must be ready to slow or stop. Look and listen for trains, obey flashing lights and gates, and never drive around lowered gates or try to beat a train across the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where are drivers prohibited from passing from either side?
options: a:Where there is a dashed white line,b:Across a combination solid and broken centerline.,c:Across a single broken yellow line.,d:Across a double solid yellow centerline.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means traffic in both directions is prohibited from crossing the line to pass. You must stay in your lane and may only cross where the markings change or where specifically allowed, such as turning into a driveway when permitted by local law.

question: Which statement about work zones is correct?
options: a:They are always marked with black-and-white signs.,b:They do not require drivers to slow down.,c:Work zones may be stationary or moving and require extra caution.,d:They are only on highways.
note: Work zones can be either stationary (like a fixed construction area) or moving (such as a line-painting or maintenance vehicle). They are typically marked with orange signs and equipment. Drivers must slow down, be prepared for sudden stops, and use extra caution because workers and unexpected lane shifts may be present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is the best practice?
options: a:Turn on hazard lights until fully merged.,b:Merge at a much slower speed than traffic.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.,d:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to freeway speed and merge smoothly.
note: When entering a freeway, use the on-ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of traffic, then merge smoothly into a safe gap. Do not stop on the ramp unless absolutely necessary, and remember that entering traffic must yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: Is it safe to use cruise control when driving on snowy or icy roads if you drive at a reduced speed?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Cruise control should not be used on snowy, icy, or otherwise slippery roads. If your tires lose traction, cruise control can keep trying to maintain speed, which may cause the wheels to spin or the vehicle to skid, making it harder to regain control.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do regarding your vehicle lights?
options: a:Drive using your parking lights,b:Use your four-way flashers instead of headlights,c:Turn on your headlights (low beams)
note: At dusk, dawn, or on overcast days, you should turn on your low-beam headlights so other drivers can see you more easily. Parking lights or hazard flashers are not a substitute for headlights while driving. Use low beams when approaching oncoming traffic or when following another vehicle closely to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: Which factors commonly cause traffic accidents?
options: a:Vehicle paint color,b:Streetlight outages,c:Inattentive driving,d:Only bad weather
note: Inattentive or distracted driving is one of the most common causes of crashes. Taking your eyes, hands, or mind off driving increases the chance of missing hazards, reacting too slowly, or making poor decisions. Other frequent causes include driving too fast for conditions and following too closely.

question: If you are being tailgated and a right lane is available, what should you do?
options: a:Ignore the tailgater and maintain exact speed.,b:Brake sharply to teach the tailgater a lesson.,c:Speed up to create more space in front of you.,d:Move to the right when safe
note: If someone is following too closely and there is a lane to your right, the safest response is to move to the right when it is safe and let them pass. This reduces the risk of a rear-end collision. Never brake suddenly to “teach a lesson,” and do not speed up; your goal is to create space and reduce conflict.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct sequence before changing lanes?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot, then change lanes when safe.,b:Check mirrors only.,c:Signal only.
note: Before changing lanes, you must signal, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, and then change lanes only when it is safe. Signaling alone is not enough; you must also make sure the lane is clear.

question: When driving on slick surfaces, what should you do regarding the vehicle ahead?
options: a:Keep the usual following distance,b:Tailgate to reduce wind effects,c:Increase your following distance,d:Speed up to pass quickly
note: On slick or slippery roads, your stopping distance increases. To give yourself more time to react and stop safely, you should increase the following distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Tailgating or keeping a normal gap is unsafe because you may not be able to stop in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A flashing red light.,c:A green arrow pointing left.,d:A steady green circular light.
note: A green left arrow is a protected turn signal, meaning oncoming traffic and pedestrians facing you are stopped, and you have the right-of-way to make the left turn. With a regular green light or flashing yellow, you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving a private road or driveway onto a sidewalk, must you stop before crossing the sidewalk?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When exiting a driveway, alley, or private road, you must stop before crossing the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians and other sidewalk users. After ensuring the sidewalk is clear, you then proceed to the street, yielding to traffic on the roadway.

question: What does a diamond-shaped sign warn drivers about?
options: a:Public recreation areas only,b:School zone only,c:Existing or possible hazards ahead,d:Regulatory information
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert drivers to existing or possible hazards or special conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, merging traffic, or work zones. They are typically yellow for general warnings and orange in construction or maintenance areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only in rural areas,b:When passing cyclists,c:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic,d:When in heavy construction zones
note: You must not drive so slowly that you block or interfere with the normal and reasonable flow of traffic, unless it is necessary for safety or required by law. Driving far below the speed of surrounding traffic without a valid reason can be illegal and may result in a citation.

question: For your own protection, which of these should you never do regarding your license?
options: a:Drive with a suspended or revoked license.,b:Always present it when requested by police.,c:Keep your license clean and legible.,d:Carry your license in a wallet.
note: Driving with a suspended or revoked license is illegal in every state and can lead to fines, arrest, and longer suspensions. You must have a valid license in your possession when driving and present it to law enforcement when requested.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians crossing a public street or highway.,b:Only cars in the same lane as you.,c:Only drivers turning left.,d:Only emergency vehicles with lights on
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians crossing a public street or highway in marked or unmarked crosswalks. You also must yield the right-of-way in other situations, such as to emergency vehicles with lights and sirens on, to vehicles already in an intersection, and when required by signs or signals, but pedestrians in the roadway are a primary right-of-way priority.

question: Which of the following best describes your responsibilities for the vehicle you drive?
options: a:Only ensure it is insured.,b:Only ensure it is properly registered.,c:Ensure it is properly registered,d:None of the above.
note: As a driver, you are responsible for making sure the vehicle you operate is properly registered, carries required insurance, and is maintained in safe operating condition. Focusing on only registration or only insurance is not enough; all legal and safety requirements must be met before you drive.

question: Can drivers park in the handicap parking access aisles beside accessible stalls?
options: a:Yes—TRUE,b:Only during certain hours,c:No—FALSE,d:Only with a permit
note: Parking in the striped access aisle next to an accessible parking space is illegal, even if you have a disability placard or plate. These aisles must stay clear so people using wheelchairs, walkers, or lifts have enough room to safely enter and exit their vehicles.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate on a two-lane road?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may pass when safe,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass
note: A double solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means no passing from either direction. You may only cross it to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road where it is legal and safe, but you must not use it for passing other vehicles.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels run off the pavement, what is the safest action?
options: a:Turn sharply left to get back on the pavement immediately.,b:Immediately brake hard and stop.,c:Accelerate and swerve back onto the road quickly.,d:Take your foot off the accelerator
note: If your right wheels leave the pavement, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and keep steering straight. Do not jerk the wheel or brake hard. After you have slowed and the car is under control, gently steer back onto the pavement when there is a safe gap in traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal displays both a red light and a green arrow, is turning in the arrow's direction prohibited until the red light changes?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, even if a red light is showing for other traffic. You may turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you need to change lanes, what steps are important?
options: a:Sound your horn and move quickly.,b:Signal ahead of the lane change and check mirrors and blind spots before moving,c:Change lanes immediately without signaling.,d:Close your eyes briefly before moving
note: Before changing lanes, signal well in advance, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move into the new lane when you are sure it is clear and you have enough space. Signaling alone is not enough; you must also check and yield to other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when meeting an oncoming vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Demand the other vehicle pull over,b:Pull completely off and stop on the other lane,c:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main-traveled portion of the road,d:Speed up to pass first
note: On a narrow road, you must share the roadway so each vehicle has about half of the main-traveled portion. Do not force the other driver off the road or speed up; slow as needed and keep as far right as is safely possible so both vehicles can pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop where two vehicles arrive at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The faster vehicle proceeds first.,b:The vehicle on the right yields to the left.,c:Both vehicles back up and wait.,d:The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
note: At a four-way stop when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps avoid confusion and collisions at intersections.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign typically indicates what?
options: a:An interstate route,b:A regulatory restriction,c:A road hazard or warning,d:A school crossing
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert drivers to road hazards, changes in road conditions, or special situations ahead, and are usually yellow or orange in work zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver's left arm and hand extended downward is the hand signal for:
options: a:Reversing the vehicle.,b:Turning right.,c:Preparing to stop.,d:Turning left.
note: Using hand signals, a left arm extended downward with the palm to the rear means the driver is slowing or stopping. Use this signal if your brake lights are not working or to give extra warning to drivers behind you.

question: In bad weather, what should drivers do to following distance?
options: a:Decrease their following distance,b:Maintain the same following distance as in clear weather,c:Increase their following distance
note: In bad weather such as rain, snow, or fog, you should increase your following distance. Extra space gives you more time to see hazards, react, and stop safely on slippery or reduced‑visibility roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it possible that 10 mph may be too fast in some conditions?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Even very low speeds like 10 mph can be too fast if conditions are poor. In heavy fog, ice, crowded parking lots, or areas with many pedestrians, you must slow down below the posted limit and drive only as fast as is safe for conditions.

question: What color are signs that indicate public recreation areas and cultural sites?
options: a:Green.,b:Orange.,c:Red.,d:Brown.
note: Brown signs are used for guidance to recreational areas, parks, historic sites, and other cultural points of interest. They help drivers find places like campgrounds, museums, and scenic areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and any traffic already in the intersection,b:Other drivers already in the intersection only,c:No one — left turns always have the right-of-way
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles, pedestrians in the crosswalk, and any traffic already in the intersection. Only turn when there is a safe gap and you will not force others to slow or stop suddenly.

question: When backing a vehicle, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Back quickly to minimize time spent reversing,b:Turn your head and look through the rear window; do not rely solely on mirrors.,c:Rely only on your mirrors.,d:Open the door to see behind you.
note: Before backing, walk around the vehicle if needed to check for children, pedestrians, or obstacles. Then back slowly while turning your head and looking through the rear window. Use mirrors and cameras only as aids, not your sole way of checking behind you.

question: Is it legal to drive around or under railroad crossing gates or barriers?
options: a:True,b:False
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive through, around, or under lowered railroad gates. You must stop when the gates are down or lights are flashing and only proceed after the signals stop and it is clearly safe to cross.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When another driver is driving slowly,b:When you are passing a bicyclist.,c:When you see a child about to run into the street.,d:When you are traveling through an intersection.
note: Use your horn only as a warning when it can help prevent a collision, such as when a child or pedestrian is about to enter your path and may not see or hear you. Do not use the horn for impatience, to scold other drivers, or in non-emergency situations.

question: Should motorists keep a safe following distance when near bicyclists?
options: a:No — treat cyclists as pedestrians.,b:Only in urban areas.,c:Only when passing on multi-lane roads.,d:Yes — always maintain a safe operating distance.
note: Always give bicyclists extra space and time. Maintain a safe following distance so you have room to react if they need to swerve to avoid hazards, slow down, or stop. Treat them as legitimate road users, not as pedestrians or obstacles.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, what must you do?
options: a:Continue driving at same speed,b:Stop in the middle of the street,c:Speed up and take the nearest exit,d:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by moving to the nearest edge or curb of the roadway and stopping until it has passed, even on a one-way street. This clears a path so the emergency vehicle can get through quickly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle using sirens and lights approaches, the driver should pull to the right-hand edge of the roadway and wait for it to pass.
options: a:False,b:True
note: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle using lights and siren, you must immediately pull as close as safely possible to the right-hand edge or curb of the road and stop, remaining stopped until the vehicle has passed. This helps emergency responders move quickly and reduces the risk of collisions.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted and driving with one hand while talking to a passenger, you should:
options: a:Flash your lights to warn them,b:Follow closely to observe them,c:Try to correct their driving,d:Give that vehicle extra space
note: If you notice a driver ahead is distracted, increase your following distance and give them extra space. A distracted driver may brake suddenly, drift in their lane, or react unpredictably, so more space gives you time to respond safely.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Directly into the oncoming headlights.,b:At the center line.,c:At the oncoming vehicle's windshield.,d:Toward the right side of the road ahead.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, you should avoid looking directly into the bright lights because they can temporarily blind you. Instead, glance toward the right side of your lane and use the edge of the road or right-side markings as a guide while still checking traffic ahead with quick glances.

question: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle you borrow, what should you do?
options: a:Familiarize yourself with the location and operation of controls and check for defects.,b:Start driving immediately because all vehicles are the same.,c:Ignore any odd noises to avoid embarrassing the owner.,d:Drive only at night to avoid others noticing.
note: Before driving any vehicle that is new to you, you should first learn where the main controls are (lights, wipers, turn signals, gear selector, parking brake, hazard lights) and check that the vehicle appears safe to operate. If you notice defects such as bad brakes, worn tires, or malfunctioning lights, they should be fixed before you drive because you are responsible for operating a safe vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what signal are they giving?
options: a:They intend to turn right.,b:They intend to turn left.,c:They intend to stop or slow.,d:They intend to turn left after stopping
note: Hand signals are used when turn signals are not working or are hard to see. A left arm extended straight out means a left turn. A left arm bent upward at the elbow means a right turn. A left arm extended downward means the driver is slowing or stopping. When you see a driver’s left arm and hand pointed downward, be prepared for them to slow or stop and adjust your speed and following distance.

question: If faced with an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, what should you do?
options: a:Pass the bicyclist quickly regardless of the oncoming car.,b:Split the difference and squeeze between both hazards.,c:Let the oncoming car pass first,d:Stop in the travel lane until both clear.
note: When you face hazards on both sides, you should not try to squeeze between them. Instead, deal with one hazard at a time. If there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, let the oncoming car pass first while you stay in your lane. After it passes and the lane is clear, move over and pass the bicyclist with plenty of space.

question: May you drive around lowered railroad gates to cross the tracks?
options: a:No—under no circumstances,b:Yes if the train has passed,c:Only if traffic is light,d:Yes when lights stop flashing
note: You must never drive around or under lowered railroad gates, even if you do not see a train or think it has already passed. Trains can be closer or moving faster than they appear, and another train may be coming on a different track. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the gates are fully raised before crossing.

question: At what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a driver age 21 or older legally intoxicated in Virginia?
options: a:0.07 percent,b:0.08 percent,c:0.09 percent
note: For drivers 21 and older in Virginia, a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is considered driving under the influence. However, you can still be charged at a lower BAC if your driving shows you are impaired.

question: What most affects your ability to stop a vehicle safely?
options: a:Your favorite driving playlist.,b:The type of radio you are listening to.,c:The color of the vehicle.,d:Road and surface conditions (e.g. wet, icy, or gravel surfaces)
note: Road and surface conditions—such as wet, icy, gravel, or uneven pavement—have a major effect on how quickly you can stop. Poor traction increases stopping distance, so you must slow down when the road surface is less than ideal.

question: What purpose do highway pavement markings serve?
options: a:Are only used in construction zones,b:Provide information and guidance to drivers,c:Are mainly decorative,d:Warn only bicyclists
note: Highway pavement markings give drivers important information: they show lane positions, indicate where passing is allowed, guide turns, and warn about conditions such as lane endings or crosswalks.

question: Should drivers continually try to improve their driving and observation skills?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Driving always involves changing traffic, road, and weather conditions. Continually improving your observation and driving skills helps you spot hazards earlier and respond more safely.

question: Is it legal to transport children under 16 in the bed of a pickup truck with a camper shell?
options: a:No—FALSE,b:Only with parental consent,c:Yes—TRUE,d:Only on private property
note: In Virginia, it is illegal to transport children under 16 in the open bed of a pickup truck on public roads, even if there is a camper shell. Children must be properly restrained inside the vehicle.

question: If you encounter an animal in the road, what should you do?
options: a:Attempt to chase it off the road.,b:Honk loudly and swerve around it quickly.,c:Pass slowly and cautiously to avoid startling it.,d:Speed up to pass before it moves.
note: When you see an animal in the road, slow down and pass very carefully. Sudden moves, loud horn use, or speeding can startle the animal and cause it to run unpredictably into your path or another lane. It is safer to reduce speed, be prepared to stop, and pass slowly only when you can do so without frightening the animal.

question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the roadway mean?
options: a:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Railroad crossing ahead.
note: Double solid yellow lines between lanes of traffic mean vehicles in both directions may not cross the lines to pass. You may cross them only when making a permitted left turn into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley, but not to overtake another vehicle.

question: Is alcohol the leading factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes?
options: a:Only in certain states,b:Only among young drivers,c:No—FALSE,d:Yes—TRUE
note: Alcohol is a major contributing factor in fatal crashes, but it is not the single leading factor in every state or every year. Other factors such as speeding, distraction, and failure to yield also play major roles. The safe takeaway is that any alcohol use seriously increases crash risk because it harms judgment, coordination, and reaction time, so you should never drive after drinking.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Always pass on the right,b:Drive directly behind them closely,c:Avoid driving alongside large vehicles and do not tailgate,d:Flash your lights at them
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots along both sides, directly behind, and sometimes directly in front of the vehicle. To stay safe, avoid driving right beside them for long periods and never follow closely. If you cannot see the driver’s mirrors, the driver probably cannot see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can a bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws be cited?
options: a:No—bicyclists are exempt,b:Only if riding in a bike lane,c:Yes—the bicyclist can be ticketed,d:They will always receive a warning
note: In all states, bicyclists on the road must generally follow the same traffic laws as drivers of motor vehicles. They must obey signals, signs, and right‑of‑way rules, and they can be stopped and ticketed for violations such as running red lights or stop signs.

question: How should you wear your seat belt shoulder strap?
options: a:Behind your back for comfort,b:Across your shoulder and chest,c:Under your arm to keep the lap belt lower
note: The shoulder belt should go over the middle of your shoulder and across your chest, with the lap belt low across your hips. Never place the shoulder belt behind your back or under your arm, because that greatly increases the risk of serious injury in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited due to safety concerns?
options: a:On hills and curves,b:At intersections,c:All of the above,d:At railroad crossings
note: Passing is especially dangerous where you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic or where other vehicles or trains may cross your path. For this reason, passing is prohibited on hills and curves with limited visibility, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.

question: When in a line of traffic crossing a railroad with no signals or gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:You always have the right-of-way,b:You can pass slower drivers on the tracks,c:You have room to clear the tracks so you won't have to stop on them,d:You may stop on the tracks if traffic backs up
note: Before you drive onto railroad tracks, you must be sure there is enough space on the far side to completely clear the tracks. Never stop on the tracks or pass another vehicle while on or near the tracks, because a train cannot stop quickly to avoid you.

question: Which tests may the DMV require when you apply for a driver license?
options: a:Vision screening, knowledge test, and road skills test as applicable.,b:Only a knowledge test.,c:Only a road skills test.,d:No tests are required under any circumstances.
note: To make sure drivers are safe and competent, DMV typically requires a vision screening and a knowledge test, and may also require a road skills test depending on the type of license and your driving history.

question: Which traffic light indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A flashing yellow light,b:A flashing red light,c:A solid yellow light,d:A steady green light
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution, watching carefully for other vehicles and pedestrians and being prepared to stop if necessary.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:The color of the drink,b:Amount of food in the stomach,c:Only the body weight of the person.,d:Only the number of drinks consumed.
note: Alcohol affects people differently based on several factors, including how much alcohol is consumed, how quickly it is consumed, body weight, sex, and whether there is food in the stomach. Food does not prevent intoxication, but it can slow the rate at which alcohol is absorbed into the bloodstream. The color of the drink does not matter, and it is never only body weight or only the number of drinks that determines impairment.

question: On a two-lane road, must drivers always stop for a stopped school bus with its lights flashing?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: On a two-lane road with no physical divider, drivers in both directions must stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, because children may be crossing the road from either side.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember trucks generally:
options: a:Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles do.,b:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.,c:Require a smaller turning radius than passenger cars.
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need more distance to come to a complete stop, especially at higher speeds or when loaded. They also have larger blind spots and need more room to turn. You should avoid cutting in front of a truck or braking suddenly when a truck is close behind you.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Maintain your current speed and keep straight,b:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal,c:Brake hard immediately
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle going straight. Do not brake hard; instead, ease your foot off the accelerator and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Once you have the vehicle under control and your speed has dropped, brake gently as needed and steer to a safe place off the road.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Back up into traffic to clear the lane.,b:Always leave it where it stopped until police arrive.,c:Move it off the traveled portion of the roadway.,d:Hide the vehicle and leave the scene.
note: If you are involved in a minor crash and your vehicle is drivable, you should move it out of the flow of traffic to the shoulder or a safe location. This helps prevent additional collisions and keeps traffic moving. Turn on your hazard lights, and never leave the scene of the accident.

question: If your vehicle has airbags, what should you do to increase safety?
options: a:Disable the airbags,b:Lean forward while driving,c:Sit as close to the steering wheel as possible,d:Wear seat belts and move your seat back at least 10 inches from the steering wheel
note: Airbags work best when used together with seat belts and proper seating position. You should always wear your seat belt and sit at least about 10 inches away from the steering wheel so the airbag can inflate safely without hitting you too hard. Tilting the steering wheel down toward your chest (not your face) also helps reduce injury if the airbag deploys.

question: How should a lap belt be positioned for proper fit?
options: a:Hidden beneath the seat,b:Buckled snugly low across your hip bones and upper thighs,c:Loose so it is comfortable
note: A lap belt should fit low and snug across your hip bones, not across your stomach. The strong bones of your hips can better withstand crash forces and help keep you from sliding under the belt. The belt should lie low on the hips and upper thighs, not high on the abdomen, to reduce the risk of internal injuries.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement indicate?
options: a:Passing is allowed for both directions.,b:Passing is allowed only uphill.,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,d:You may cross to pass whenever traffic is light.
note: Two solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean no passing from either direction. You must stay in your lane and may not cross the lines to pass. You may cross them only when making a left turn into or out of a driveway or side road, if it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

question: Which kinds of drugs can impair driving ability?
options: a:Only illegal drugs,b:Only alcohol,c:Prescription and over-the-counter medications,d:Only prescription drugs
note: Many types of drugs can impair driving, including prescription medications, over‑the‑counter medicines, and illegal drugs. Some can make you drowsy, slow your reactions, or affect your judgment and coordination. Always read labels and talk to your doctor or pharmacist about side effects before driving after taking any medication.

question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign typically:
options: a:Warns you about conditions on or near the road.,b:Directs you to nearby cities.,c:Gives regulatory rules like speed limits.,d:Indicates a rest area ahead.
note: Yellow and black diamond‑shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to upcoming road conditions or hazards such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or changes in road width or surface so you can slow down and proceed with caution.

question: If you stop along the road at night, which lights should you use?
options: a:Use only parking lights,b:Turn on emergency flashers and keep low beam headlights on,c:Use high beams,d:Turn off all lights
note: If you must stop along the road at night, you want your vehicle to be as visible as possible without blinding others. Turn on your emergency flashers so your car is clearly marked as stopped, and keep your low beam headlights on so approaching drivers can see you and the area around your vehicle.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane adjacent to the broken line.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,c:Passing is allowed in both directions.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. Passing is allowed only for drivers in the lane next to the broken line. Drivers in the lane next to the solid line must not cross it to pass.

question: What does Virginia's zero tolerance law for drivers under 21 mean?
options: a:Drivers under 21 are allowed up to 0.08% BAC.,b:It applies only to commercial drivers.,c:It is illegal for those under 21 to drive with a BAC of 0.02% or higher.,d:It means no alcohol-related laws apply to teens.
note: Under Virginia’s zero tolerance law, drivers under 21 may not drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02% or higher. Because people under 21 are not allowed to drink at all, the law sets a very low BAC limit to discourage any drinking before driving.

question: What are Virginia's curfew hours for drivers under 18?
options: a:Midnight until 4 a.m.,b:8 p.m. until midnight,c:10 p.m. until 2 a.m.,d:9 p.m. until 1 a.m.
note: In Virginia, drivers under 18 generally may not drive between midnight and 4 a.m. This curfew is intended to reduce crashes during late-night hours when fatigue and impaired drivers are more common. Limited exceptions apply, such as driving to or from work or a school-sponsored activity.

question: Which in-vehicle activity increases crash risk the most?
options: a:Using a cell phone,b:Listening to the radio,c:Adjusting AC temperature,d:Looking in your rearview mirror briefly
note: Using a cell phone while driving is one of the most dangerous in‑vehicle distractions because it takes your eyes, hands, and mind away from driving. Even hands‑free use can significantly reduce your attention to the road, increasing your risk of a crash more than routine tasks like adjusting controls or checking mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
