question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When your signal is a green arrow,b:When another vehicle is on a road to your right and you arrive at an unmarked intersection at the same time,c:When you are entering a street from a garage
note: At an unmarked intersection, you must yield to vehicles that arrive first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. A green arrow means you may proceed in the direction of the arrow, but only after yielding to any traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection. When entering a street from a garage, driveway, or alley, you must also yield to traffic and pedestrians. Because all three listed situations require yielding, the question should ask when you must yield in each listed situation, or the options should be rewritten so only one is correct.

question: Traffic lanes moving in opposite directions are divided by what color lines?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Red
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and red is not used to separate lanes of opposing traffic.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It reduces your fuel consumption.,b:It prevents other drivers from changing lanes.,c:It gives you time to react to unexpected actions by other road users.,d:It keeps traffic flowing faster.
note: Maintaining a space cushion gives you extra time and distance to react if another driver brakes suddenly, changes lanes, or makes a mistake. This buffer zone reduces the chance of a collision and allows smoother, safer driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If approaching a stop sign without a marked crosswalk, must you stop before entering the intersection?
options: a:False,b:True
note: At a stop sign with no marked crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection, at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic. You may need to stop again as you move forward to get a better view, but you must not roll into the intersection without first stopping.

question: How should you prepare for hazards on the road ahead?
options: a:Stare straight ahead at all times.,b:Drive with your left foot resting on the brake.,c:Continually scan the entire roadway and roadsides.,d:Focus only on the vehicle directly ahead
note: Continually scanning the road ahead, to the sides, and checking mirrors helps you spot hazards early, such as slowing traffic, pedestrians, or vehicles entering from side streets. Early detection gives you more time to adjust speed or position safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light turns green, what must you do before proceeding?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to any pedestrians or vehicles legally in the intersection.,b:Back up to recheck the intersection.,c:Honk to alert others you are moving.,d:Accelerate as fast as possible.
note: A green light means you may go, but only after you first check the intersection and yield to any pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles already in the intersection. They have the right-of-way and you must let them clear before you proceed.

question: When are roads most slippery during a rainstorm?
options: a:During the first 10 to 15 minutes.,b:After it has been raining for hours.,c:Only when temperatures are below freezing,d:The day after it rains.
note: Roads are usually most slippery during the first 10–15 minutes of a rainstorm because water mixes with oil, grease, and other residue on the surface. This creates a slick layer that increases the risk of skidding until the rain washes it away.

question: When driving in traffic, it is safest to:
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic at a reasonable speed.,b:Drive much faster than other vehicles to pass quickly.,c:Drive much slower than the flow to be cautious.,d:Constantly change lanes to find gaps.
note: It is safest to drive at a speed that matches the flow of traffic while staying within the posted speed limit and adjusting for conditions. Driving much faster or much slower than surrounding traffic increases the chance of conflicts and collisions.

question: A flashing yellow arrow for left turns means you may:
options: a:Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Turn left only when the intersection is empty.,c:Come to a complete stop before turning.
note: A flashing yellow arrow for a left turn means you may turn left, but only after yielding to oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians. Oncoming traffic has the right-of-way, and you must wait for a safe gap before turning.

question: Do ramps and bridges tend to freeze before roadways?
options: a:True — ramps and bridges can freeze sooner than roads.,b:False — they freeze at the same time.,c:They never freeze before roads.,d:Only rural roads freeze first.
note: Ramps and bridges often freeze before the rest of the roadway because they are exposed to cold air from above and below. This allows their surface temperature to drop faster, causing ice to form even when nearby roads may still be just wet.

question: If you have a tire blowout while driving, which is the correct sequence of actions?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas, avoid heavy braking, slow gradually, then pull off.,b:Brake hard immediately and steer to the shoulder.,c:Speed up to reach a safe area quickly.,d:Turn the steering wheel sharply and stop in the travel lane.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, ease your foot off the accelerator, avoid hard braking, let the vehicle slow down gradually, then signal and steer off the road when you have control.

question: Which action can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Using improper turn signals,b:Disobeying posted speed limits,c:Allowing extra travel time
note: Allowing extra travel time helps you stay calm, avoid rushing, and reduces the temptation to speed, tailgate, or make aggressive maneuvers that can lead to road rage.

question: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as which sign?
options: a:Solid red light.,b:Stop sign.,c:Yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign, and then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: Do you have to stop for a school bus on a private road when its red lights are flashing?
options: a:True,b:False
note: In most U.S. states, you must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm on both public and private roads, unless you are on the opposite side of a divided highway where stopping is not required by local law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians,b:Maintain a normal driving speed without stopping,c:Stop and check for nearby police cars first
note: When turning right on a green light, you may proceed if not prohibited by signs, but you must always yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any traffic already in or close to the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on Virginia interstates in designated rural areas?
options: a:50 mph.,b:70 mph.,c:60 mph.
note: On certain rural interstate segments in Virginia, the maximum posted speed limit is 70 mph unless signs show a lower limit. Always obey the posted speed limit, as it may be lower in some areas due to conditions or design.

question: Which practices improve night driving safety?
options: a:Drive faster to get through dark areas quickly.,b:Keep interior lights on brightly,c:Use parking lights instead of headlights.,d:Increase following distance and ensure headlights work properly.
note: At night, you should increase your following distance so you have more time to react, and make sure your headlights and other lights are clean and working properly. Do not drive faster to “get through” dark areas, avoid using bright interior lights, and always use proper headlights rather than just parking lights.

question: Which statement about passing motorcycles is true?
options: a:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle,b:It is okay to pass a motorcycle by mildly overlapping lanes,c:You may pass a motorcycle in a bike lane,d:Motorcycles do not require the full lane width
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other motor vehicle. When passing, you must move completely into the adjacent lane and pass as you would another car, leaving plenty of space and not sharing or overlapping the lane.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, how should you safely pass a bicyclist traveling the same direction?
options: a:Continue straight — the bicyclist should get out of your way,b:Only pass at a traffic signal or stop sign,c:Slow down and pass only when you can give at least 3 feet of clearance and it is safe to do so
note: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, slow down and pass a bicyclist only when it is safe, just as you would pass a slow-moving vehicle. Make sure you have a clear view of oncoming traffic, allow at least 3 feet of space (or more if possible), and do not pass if you cannot give enough room or see clearly ahead.

question: If a vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) starts to lose traction, what should you do?
options: a:Press and hold the gas pedal,b:Pump the brakes,c:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer where you want to go
note: With ABS, you should press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer where you want to go. The ABS system automatically pumps the brakes to help prevent wheel lockup, so you can maintain steering control. Do not pump the brakes yourself in a vehicle equipped with ABS.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Turn off brake lights when stopping,b:Brake abruptly to warn others,c:Avoid sudden stops and slow down gradually,d:Speed up to clear intersections
note: To help prevent rear-end collisions, avoid sudden stops whenever possible. Ease off the accelerator early and apply your brakes smoothly so your brake lights come on in time for drivers behind you to see and react. Gradual slowing gives following drivers more distance and time to stop safely.

question: Which action should you take just before making a turn?
options: a:Brake abruptly just prior to turning.,b:Increase your speed to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Activate your turn signal several seconds before turning.,d:Begin turning without signaling if traffic is light.
note: Before making a turn, you should signal well in advance—typically at least 100 feet or about three to four seconds before turning. Using your turn signal early lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you plan to do so they can adjust their speed or position safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which pavement marking allows you to pass into the adjacent lane?
options: a:Broken white line.,b:Solid yellow line.,c:Double solid white line.,d:Double solid yellow line.
note: A broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and you may cross it when it is safe to change lanes or pass. Solid yellow or double yellow lines generally mean no passing, and double solid white lines usually mean you should not change lanes.

question: If you discover a defect that may affect safe operation of your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Only fix it when you get a warning light on the dash.,b:Have it corrected as soon as possible before driving.,c:Continue driving until it breaks down completely.,d:Ignore it if driving a short distance.
note: If you find a defect that could affect the safe operation of your vehicle—such as problems with brakes, steering, tires, or lights—you should have it repaired as soon as possible and avoid driving the vehicle until it is fixed. Driving with known safety defects increases your risk of a crash and may be illegal.

question: At intersections with light rail, what must drivers always do?
options: a:Assume trains always yield to vehicles.,b:Obey all traffic signals and look both ways before crossing tracks.,c:Ignore pedestrian presence near tracks.,d:Drive around lowered crossing gates.
note: At intersections with light rail, you must always obey all traffic signals and signs and look both ways along the tracks before crossing. Trains are large, take a long distance to stop, and may be quieter than expected, so you must never assume they will yield to you or drive around lowered gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before passing other vehicles?
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots,b:Re-enter the lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,c:Honk at the vehicle ahead before passing.,d:Pass on the shoulder if traffic is slow
note: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots, signal, and make sure there is enough clear space to pass safely. After passing, only move back into your original lane when you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: What is the safest way to transport small children in a vehicle?
options: a:Hold them in an adult's lap,b:Secure them in an appropriate child safety seat,c:Allow them to stand on the floor in the back
note: Small children must always be secured in an age‑ and size‑appropriate child safety seat or booster seat in the back seat. In a crash, an adult cannot hold a child safely, even at low speeds.

question: Which of the following can be penalties for a DUI conviction?
options: a:License suspension or revocation,b:All of the above,c:Fines and restitution,d:Jail time
note: A DUI conviction can lead to license suspension or revocation, fines and other financial costs, and possible jail time. Penalties vary by state and by the circumstances, but all of these consequences are possible.

question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog?
options: a:True,b:False
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back at you, making it harder to see the road ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal displays a steady green arrow for your lane, you may:
options: a:Continue straight only.,b:Ignore other signs or lane markings.,c:Turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.,d:Turn without checking for other vehicles or pedestrians.
note: A steady green arrow means you have a protected turn in that direction, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection before you complete your turn.

question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,b:Look only at the rearview mirror.,c:Use your turn signal and assume it's clear,d:Rely solely on the left side mirror.
note: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Mirrors alone cannot show areas directly beside and slightly behind your vehicle, so a quick shoulder check plus mirror use is essential for safe lane changes.

question: Is nighttime the safest time for cyclists to ride?
options: a:Only when wearing reflective gear,b:No—FALSE,c:Yes—TRUE,d:Only in well-lit areas
note: Nighttime is generally more dangerous for cyclists because they are harder for drivers to see, even with lights and reflective gear. Drivers must be extra alert for bicycles at night, and cyclists should use proper lighting and reflective clothing, but night is not the safest time to ride.

question: What do pennant-shaped road signs indicate?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:No passing zones.,c:School zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs are used specifically for "No Passing Zone" warnings. They are usually placed on the left side of the road to tell drivers that passing other vehicles is unsafe and illegal in that area.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Work harder to steer and gradually slow down to pull off the road safely.,b:Turn on hazard lights, steer firmly, and move off the road.,c:Honk your horn and shift to neutral while steering to the side of the road.
note: If power steering fails, the steering wheel will become much harder to turn, but you can still steer the vehicle. Firmly grip the wheel, steer with extra effort, gradually slow down, and move to the side of the road when it is safe. Turn on your hazard lights once you are slowing or stopped to alert other drivers.

question: If there are two parallel railroad tracks, what precaution should you take?
options: a:Honk and drive around any remaining gates.,b:After one train passes, make sure all tracks are clear before crossing.,c:Assume the crossing is safe once one train passes.,d:Cross immediately as the first train clears.
note: At crossings with more than one track, always check for another train before crossing. After one train passes, look and listen carefully in both directions and make sure all tracks are clear before you start across; another train may be approaching on a different track.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian walk on?
options: a:On the same side of the road on which traffic is moving.,b:On the side of the road facing oncoming traffic.,c:On the side of the road which has the lightest traffic.
note: On roads without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on the side facing oncoming traffic. This lets them see approaching vehicles and react if a driver is not paying attention, and it also makes them more visible to drivers.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will touch the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before a turn should you signal when preparing to turn?
options: a:200 feet.,b:About 100 feet (three to four seconds).,c:50 feet.,d:Immediately before turning
note: In most areas, you should signal at least 100 feet before turning in city or town driving. This is about three to four seconds before the turn and gives other road users enough time to see and react to your intentions.

question: Are drivers allowed to pass a school bus that is displaying flashing red lights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When a school bus has flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, drivers in both directions must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. The main exception is traffic on the opposite side of a divided highway with a physical median, which is usually not required to stop.

question: If a pedestrian begins crossing in front of you, what is the proper response?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop,b:Flash your lights to warn them.,c:Speed up and pass in front of them.,d:Sound your horn repeatedly
note: If a pedestrian starts to cross in front of you, you must yield. Slow down and be prepared to stop, giving the pedestrian enough time and space to cross safely. Never speed up, try to pass in front of them, or rely on your horn or lights to make them move.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A “No stopping” sign means you may stop only to:
options: a:Unload packages at any time,b:Discharge passengers whenever you wish,c:Avoid a conflict with other traffic
note: A 'No stopping' zone means you may not stop your vehicle there for any reason except when it is absolutely necessary to safely keep traffic moving and avoid danger. You may stop only long enough to obey a traffic signal or sign, follow a police officer’s directions, or avoid a collision or conflict with other traffic. You may not stop to load or unload passengers or cargo.

question: When sharing the road with a motorcycle, what must you do?
options: a:Force the motorcycle to use half a lane.,b:Pass the motorcycle within the same lane.,c:Drive beside the motorcycle in the same lane.,d:Allow the motorcycle the full width of a travel lane.
note: A motorcycle is entitled to a full lane, just like a car. Never try to share the same lane side‑by‑side with a motorcycle or crowd it to one side. Allow the motorcycle the full width of the lane so the rider has room to maneuver around hazards and maintain balance.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Reach down and try to pull the pedal up.,b:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.,c:Shift to park immediately.,d:Turn off the radio and continue driving
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral, and apply steady pressure on the brakes. Steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place. Once stopped, turn off the engine. Do not reach down to pull up the pedal while moving, and do not shift to park until the vehicle is fully stopped, as this can damage the transmission or cause loss of control.

question: Many crashes are caused by which of the following?
options: a:Driving too fast for conditions,b:Consistently checking mirrors and blind spots,c:Yielding the right-of-way
note: Driving too fast for conditions is a major cause of crashes. Even if you are at or below the posted speed limit, you must slow down when roads are wet, icy, or gravel, when visibility is poor, or when traffic is heavy. Safe speed is the speed that allows you to stop and react in time for hazards, not just the number on the sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, what must you ensure before passing?
options: a:You exceed the speed limit while passing,b:You honk before passing.,c:That the passing lane is clear.,d:You pass only on the right.
note: On a multilane highway, you must be sure the passing lane is clear before you move over. Check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, signal, and then change lanes only when it is safe. Do not exceed the speed limit while passing, and normally pass on the left unless specific conditions or signs allow a safe right‑side pass.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:Alcohol improves nighttime vision.,b:Only very high BAC levels affect driving.,c:Alcohol has no effect on driving skills.,d:Even a small amount of alcohol can impair concentration
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can slow your reaction time, reduce your ability to judge distances and speeds, and make it harder to concentrate. You do not need to be legally drunk for your driving to be impaired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you do safely and legally?
options: a:Use the shoulder to pass,b:Flash your lights at oncoming traffic,c:Move into the oncoming traffic lane to complete the pass only where passing is permitted and you have enough clear distance
note: On a two-lane, two-way road, you must move into the oncoming traffic lane to pass, but only when passing is permitted by the road markings and signs, you have enough clear distance to complete the pass safely, and you can return to your lane without interfering with oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit in residential, school, or business zones unless posted otherwise?
options: a:30 mph.,b:35 mph.,c:25 mph in many residential and business areas when not otherwise posted (school zones often have special posted limits).,d:15 mph.
note: Unless a different limit is posted, the speed limit in these zones is 25 mph for passenger vehicles and motorcycles.

question: At night, which is most difficult to see?
options: a:Road signs.,b:Pedestrians.,c:Other motorists.
note: Pedestrians are much harder to see at night than reflective road signs or vehicles with lights. Because they may wear dark clothing and are not illuminated, you must scan carefully, especially near crosswalks and along the road edge.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog because their light aims down toward the road and causes less glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in fog and can bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal displays a steady yellow arrow for a turn, what should drivers do?
options: a:Slow to a stop if it is safe to do so,b:Merge into the lane indicated by the arrow,c:Proceed with the turn after yielding
note: A steady yellow turn arrow means the protected turning movement is ending and a red arrow is coming. You should slow and prepare to stop before the intersection, and stop if you can do so safely. Only continue through the turn if you are already in the intersection or cannot safely stop in time.

question: Which action most helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Get off highways immediately no matter the situation.,b:Drive with your hazard lights on constantly.,c:Engage four-wheel drive and maintain normal speed.,d:Reduce speed and increase following distance.
note: On icy or snowy roads, traction is greatly reduced, so you need more time and space to react. Reducing your speed and increasing your following distance gives your tires a better chance to grip the road and allows more room to brake and steer smoothly, which helps prevent skids and collisions.

question: When is it required to use your turn signal?
options: a:You must signal when pulling into or out of a parking space.,b:You must signal when turning at an intersection.,c:You must signal when changing lanes.
note: Turn signals are required whenever you change direction or move your vehicle laterally, including changing lanes, turning at intersections, and entering or leaving a parking space, curb, driveway, or alley. Signaling lets other road users anticipate your movements and reduces the risk of crashes.

question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do first to warn them?
options: a:Wave your arms out the window.,b:Sound your horn to alert the other driver.,c:Flash your interior dome light.,d:Turn off your headlights.
note: If another vehicle is about to collide with you, your horn is the quickest and most effective way to warn the other driver. A sharp blast on the horn can get their attention immediately so they may brake or steer away to avoid or lessen the impact.

question: Which of the following is least likely to be a direct recommendation for safer night driving?
options: a:Being aware that tinted windows reduce nighttime visibility,b:Keeping your windshield clean,c:Carrying a flashlight in your vehicle
note: Safe night driving focuses on seeing and being seen: keeping the windshield clean to reduce glare, using headlights properly, and understanding that tinted windows can further reduce visibility in the dark. Carrying a flashlight can be helpful if you are stopped or stranded, but it is not a primary driving technique for safer night driving.

question: Which is a safe way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Speed up entering the curve and slow down as you exit.,b:Maintain maximum speed throughout the curve.,c:Slow down before entering the curve and accelerate gradually as you exit.
note: Slow down before entering a curve so you can steer smoothly and keep traction. Once you are safely in the curve and can see the road ahead, you can gradually accelerate as you exit to stabilize the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the usual speed limit in a school zone unless otherwise posted?
options: a:Varies by state law and posted signs,b:15 mph.,c:25 mph.,d:20 mph.
note: School zone speed limits are set by each state and often vary between about 15–25 mph, and they are almost always specifically posted with signs and sometimes flashing lights. You must obey the posted school zone speed limit; do not assume it is the same as the general residential or business district limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the left.,b:The faster vehicle.,c:The vehicle on the right.,d:The vehicle that honks first.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Yielding to the vehicle on your right helps prevent confusion and collisions.

question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection with working lights, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn,b:Follow the officer's directions,c:Obey the traffic lights instead,d:Ignore both and proceed
note: When a police officer or other authorized person is directing traffic, their hand signals and directions override traffic lights and signs. Always follow the officer’s directions, even if the traffic signal shows a different indication.

question: What characterizes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Always drives slowly regardless of conditions,b:Anticipates the actions of other drivers,c:Never changes speed,d:Relies exclusively on other drivers to be cautious
note: A good defensive driver stays alert, watches other road users, and anticipates what they might do. By expecting possible mistakes from others and adjusting speed and position early, defensive drivers reduce the chance of a collision.

question: Does vehicle speed affect stopping distance?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Vehicle speed has a major effect on stopping distance. As speed increases, both your reaction distance (how far you travel before you start braking) and your braking distance (how far it takes to stop once you brake) increase. This means higher speeds require much more space and time to stop safely.

question: If stopped by a police officer, what should you do?
options: a:Retrieve your documents before the officer arrives,b:Exit the vehicle immediately and approach the officer.,c:Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the wheel and wait for the officer.,d:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window before they reach you.
note: If stopped by police, slow down and pull over safely, then stay in your vehicle unless the officer instructs otherwise. Keep your hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer’s directions before reaching for documents. This helps the officer see that you are not a threat and keeps everyone safer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When anything makes conditions less than perfect,b:Only when you see a police officer,c:When entering a highway where there are other cars
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum allowed in ideal conditions, not a required speed. You must slow down below the limit whenever conditions are less than perfect—such as rain, snow, fog, heavy traffic, poor road surfaces, or limited visibility—so that you can stop safely and maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:Night driving.,b:High speeds.,c:Low tire pressure,d:Slow speeds.
note: High speeds greatly increase how far you need to stop and how severe a crash will be. As speed goes up, your braking distance grows much faster than your speed, and the force of impact in a collision rises sharply. Driving at safer speeds gives you more time to react and reduces crash severity.

question: Must you yield to children playing in the street?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must always be prepared to yield to pedestrians, including children playing in or near the street, even if they are not in a crosswalk. Children can be unpredictable and may suddenly run into the road. In residential areas and near schools or playgrounds, slow down, watch carefully, and be ready to stop to avoid hitting a child.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn, what should you do with your speed?
options: a:Reduce your speed to maintain control.,b:Maintain or vary as you like.,c:Come to a stop and then accelerate speedily,d:Increase your speed.
note: Reduce your speed before and during a turn so you can keep control of the vehicle, stay in your lane, and react to hazards. Entering a turn too fast makes it harder to steer smoothly and can cause skidding.

question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates what?
options: a:A solid white line is not normally used as the center line between opposite directions; white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and a solid white line discourages or prohibits lane changes.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass (this would normally be shown by a solid yellow center line),c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe (this would normally be shown by a broken yellow center line)
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction; yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A solid white line between same‑direction lanes means lane changes are discouraged or prohibited, depending on state law and signs. A solid line down the center of a two‑lane road that separates opposing traffic would normally be yellow, not white.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond when you see a yield sign at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and yield to traffic in the road you are entering.,b:Always come to a complete stop regardless of traffic.,c:Yield only to traffic on your left.,d:Proceed without slowing if no traffic is visible
note: At a yield sign, slow down and be prepared to stop. You must let vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection go first. If traffic or pedestrians are present, stop if needed and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Lack of sleep affects your driving similar to which of the following?
options: a:The effect that anger has,b:The effect that amphetamines have,c:The effect that alcohol has
note: Driving while very tired slows your reaction time, harms judgment, and reduces awareness in ways similar to alcohol. Being awake for many hours can impair you about as much as having a moderate or even illegal blood alcohol concentration, making drowsy driving very dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when a traffic signal shows a steady red arrow?
options: a:Stop,b:Slow and proceed with caution without stopping.,c:Turn immediately if no pedestrians are present.,d:Come to a full stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.
note: A steady red arrow means you must come to a complete stop and stay stopped in the direction of the arrow until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a posted sign specifically allows a turn on red after stopping and yielding.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Following closely to prevent cut-offs.,b:Driving only during daylight hours,c:Identifying dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.,d:Getting ahead of poor drivers to stay safe.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road, spotting potential hazards early, and adjusting your speed, position, or actions to avoid collisions. Instead of reacting at the last second, you plan ahead and leave yourself space and time to respond safely.

question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?
options: a:Speed up to increase distance from them.,b:Slam on your brakes to scare them away.,c:Ignore them and maintain speed,d:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.
note: When someone is following too closely, the safest response is to create space and let them pass. Signal and change lanes when it is safe, or gradually slow down so they can go around you. Avoid sudden braking or speeding up, which can increase the risk of a rear-end crash or road rage.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A circular green sign,b:A rectangular red sign,c:A reflective orange triangle with a red border
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle with a red border mounted on the rear of vehicles that usually travel 25 mph or less, such as farm equipment. When you see this emblem, reduce speed early and be prepared to pass only when it is safe and legal.

question: Is it safe to stop on railroad tracks for a short time when moving with a stream of vehicles?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must never stop on railroad tracks, even briefly. Before crossing, make sure there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle so you will not be forced to stop on the tracks. If traffic is backed up, wait before the tracks until you can clear them completely.

question: What must a professional truck driver have to operate commercial vehicles?
options: a:Ownership of an 18-wheeler,b:A regular driver's license only,c:A fishing license,d:A valid commercial driver's license (CDL)
note: Driving large or certain types of commercial vehicles requires a Commercial Driver’s License (CDL). A CDL involves additional testing and qualifications beyond a regular driver’s license to ensure drivers can safely handle the size, weight, and special equipment of commercial vehicles.

question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:As a stop sign—come to a complete stop,b:Ignore it,c:Only stop if police are present,d:Proceed without stopping if no traffic is present
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: In Virginia, when transporting anyone under 18, what must the driver ensure?
options: a:All passengers under 18 are properly secured by seat belts or child safety seats,b:Only passengers under 8 must be belted,c:It is the passenger's responsibility,d:Only front-seat passengers under 18 must be belted
note: In Virginia, the driver is legally responsible for making sure all passengers under 18 are properly secured with seat belts or appropriate child safety seats, no matter where they sit in the vehicle.

question: When dealing with pedestrians, what is a driver's responsibility?
options: a:Require pedestrians to always yield,b:Yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians and do everything possible to avoid striking them,c:Only watch for pedestrians at marked crosswalks,d:Yell at pedestrians to stay out of the road
note: Drivers must always watch for pedestrians and yield the right‑of‑way when required. Even if a pedestrian is crossing improperly, you must do everything you can to avoid hitting them.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing where you see no train, when must you still stop?
options: a:If crossing gate is lowered or lights are flashing,b:All of the above,c:If a stop sign is posted,d:If a flagger signals you to stop
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when the gates are down, warning lights are flashing, a stop sign is posted, or a flagger signals you to stop, even if you do not see a train yet.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're traveling slower than other traffic on a multilane roadway, you must:
options: a:Stay in the middle lane.,b:Drive in the right-hand lane.,c:Not change lanes.,d:None of the above.
note: On multilane roads, slower traffic should keep right. Staying in the right‑hand lane lets faster vehicles pass safely on the left and helps traffic flow smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to exceed the speed limit when passing another vehicle?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must obey the posted speed limit at all times. Passing another vehicle is not a valid reason to exceed the speed limit; you should only pass when you can do so safely while staying at or below the limit.

question: When should you slow down?
options: a:When entering a highway with other cars,b:Only when a police car is present,c:When the road is wet or slippery,d:On narrow or winding roads, near intersections or crossings, on hills and curves, where pedestrians are present, and when roads are wet or slippery
note: You should slow down whenever conditions reduce visibility or traction, such as on wet or slippery roads, narrow or winding roads, near intersections and crossings, on hills and curves, and where pedestrians are present. Slower speeds give you more time and distance to react safely.

question: If a railroad crossing has no warning devices, you should slow down, look, and listen before proceeding.
options: a:True,b:False
note: At a railroad crossing without gates, lights, or bells, you must slow down, look carefully in both directions, and listen for trains before crossing. Only proceed when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to fully clear the tracks.

question: To relieve fatigue on a long trip, which is recommended?
options: a:Drive with one eye closed to rest the other,b:Only take caffeine to stay alert,c:Keep driving and play loud music,d:Stop and rest about every two hours
note: On long trips, stop about every two hours to rest, stretch, and refresh yourself. If you feel drowsy, pull over in a safe place and rest. Relying on caffeine, loud music, or other tricks is not a safe substitute for real rest.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, how should you steer?
options: a:Overcorrect the steering to regain control,b:Turn your wheel into traffic,c:Turn your steering wheel in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, which is usually the same direction the rear is skidding. This helps you straighten the vehicle. Avoid slamming on the brakes or making sudden, sharp steering corrections, as these can make the skid worse.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn, where should your vehicle be positioned?
options: a:Near the center of the street,b:As close to the right side of the roadway as possible,c:Close to the left side of the street
note: For a right turn, you should be in the lane closest to the right edge or curb, and as near to the right side of that lane as is safe. This shortens your turn, keeps you predictable to other drivers, and reduces the chance of sideswipes or cutting across other lanes.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Human error,b:Bad weather,c:New drivers,d:Vehicle defects
note: Most crashes are caused by human error, such as inattention, distraction, following too closely, speeding, or misjudging gaps. Weather and vehicle defects can contribute, but they account for far fewer crashes than driver behavior.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires the same action as which device?
options: a:A stop sign,b:A slow sign,c:A speed limit sign,d:A yield sign
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, yield to any traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe—just as you would at a stop sign.

question: Are motorists required to yield to pedestrians who walk against the traffic light?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must always exercise due care to avoid hitting pedestrians, even when the pedestrian is crossing against the signal or outside a crosswalk. You may not have to give them the legal right‑of‑way, but you must still slow or stop if necessary to avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are drivers required to yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When a pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk, drivers must slow or stop as needed to let the pedestrian cross safely. Many states also require yielding to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks at intersections when there are no traffic signals.

question: Where are you prohibited from parking?
options: a:In a parking lot,b:On a hill,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane
note: Parking on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane is illegal because it blocks pedestrians and cyclists and creates a safety hazard. Many other locations are also prohibited, such as near fire hydrants, intersections, and railroad crossings. Parking lots and hills are not automatically prohibited as long as you follow posted signs and do not create a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind while driving uphill, what should you expect about the truck's speed?
options: a:You may not be able to legally pass the truck,b:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit,c:You may be able to pass at any time
note: Large trucks are heavy and lose speed on uphill grades, so they often travel slower than the posted speed limit when climbing. You should expect this and be prepared to slow down. Only pass if it is legal and safe, with enough clear distance and visibility; never assume you can pass at any time on a hill.

question: What causes “highway hypnosis”?
options: a:Too much sleep before driving,b:Getting frequent rest breaks,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods
note: Highway hypnosis happens when a driver stares straight ahead at the road for long periods and stops actively scanning mirrors, signs, and surrounding traffic. This reduces alertness and awareness, making it easier to miss slowing or stopped vehicles and other hazards. Taking breaks and changing your focus regularly helps prevent it.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks on a busy street, what should you do?
options: a:Keep accelerating and hope it stops,b:Slam on the brakes repeatedly until the engine stalls,c:Jump out of the moving vehicle,d:Shift to neutral, steer to safety, then turn off the ignition without locking the steering
note: If the accelerator sticks, shift to neutral first to disconnect the engine from the wheels, then steer to keep control, apply the brakes, and move to a safe place off the road. Once you are in neutral and under control, you can turn off the ignition without locking the steering. Never jump from a moving vehicle or keep accelerating.

question: What should be your first response to decreased visibility while driving?
options: a:Open your windows for fresh air.,b:Flash your high beams.,c:Reduce your speed.,d:Turn on your windshield wipers only.
note: When visibility decreases, your first response should be to reduce your speed so you have more time to see and react to hazards. After slowing down, use your low-beam headlights and windshield wipers as needed so you can see and be seen. Do not rely on high beams in fog or heavy precipitation, as they can make visibility worse.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required at an intersection but no stop line or crosswalk is visible, where should you stop?
options: a:Stop at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic.,b:You are not required to stop.,c:Slow down but do not stop unless you see cross traffic.
note: When there is a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk, you must still make a complete stop. Stop at the point just before entering the intersection where you can see traffic on the intersecting road, without moving into the cross street.

question: Why must you be especially careful near a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They may be deaf.,b:They are a police officer.,c:They are blind or visually impaired.
note: A white cane (with or without a red tip) or a guide dog identifies a pedestrian as blind or visually impaired. You must slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop to allow them to cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right,b:Either one may proceed first,c:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the best response?
options: a:Flash lights and honk repeatedly,b:Retaliate by speeding up,c:Block their vehicle from passing,d:Stay calm and move out of their way
note: If another driver acts aggressively or cuts you off, the safest response is to stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and create space by slowing down or changing lanes when safe. Do not retaliate, as that can escalate road rage and increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When stopped in a travel lane, are you allowed to stop to drop off passengers or look up an address?
options: a:Only if you flash your hazards first.,b:Only during off-peak hours.,c:No — do not stop in a travel lane; pull off the road to do such tasks.,d:Yes — stopping in a travel lane is acceptable.
note: Travel lanes are for moving traffic only. Do not stop in a travel lane to drop off passengers, check directions, or for other non-emergency reasons. Continue driving until you can safely pull off the roadway or into a legal parking area.

question: How should drivers treat traffic signs and pavement markings?
options: a:They apply only when other traffic is present.,b:They are optional at night,c:They must always be obeyed.,d:They are merely suggestions.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal controls, not suggestions. They apply at all times, regardless of traffic, time of day, or weather, and must be obeyed to maintain safe and orderly traffic flow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.,b:After slowing to check for traffic only if cars are present.,c:Without stopping if no pedestrians are visible,d:After coming to a complete stop before entering and verifying it is safe to proceed.
note: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection. After stopping, look for traffic and pedestrians in all directions and proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: At what minimum BAC are drivers 21 and older legally considered to be driving under the influence?
options: a:0.08 percent.,b:0.10 percent.,c:0.06 percent.,d:0.02 percent.
note: For drivers 21 and older in most U.S. states, including Virginia, a BAC of 0.08% or higher is the legal per se limit for DUI. However, any amount of alcohol can impair driving, and you can be unsafe to drive even below 0.08%.

question: How should you behave when near a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Take the right-of-way,b:Proceed normally; they will yield,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop,d:Honk to alert them
note: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must yield the right-of-way, slow down, and be prepared to stop. Do not honk, which can startle them, and never insist on your right-of-way. Give them extra time and space to cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you find yourself driving in another driver's blind spot, what is the safest action?
options: a:Stay in the blind spot until the other driver changes lanes,b:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you,c:Remain at the same speed and position,d:Change lanes abruptly without signaling
note: A blind spot is an area another driver cannot see in their mirrors. If you stay there, they may change lanes into you. Either gently speed up to move ahead or slow down to fall back so you are clearly visible in their mirrors.

question: Which action best helps you avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Call a taxi only after you start drinking,b:Simply say “No thanks,c:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive
note: Deciding before you drink that you will not drive is the safest strategy because alcohol impairs judgment and self-control. Once you have been drinking, you are more likely to underestimate your level of impairment and make poor decisions about driving. Planning ahead—such as arranging a sober driver or alternate transportation—prevents you from driving under the influence.

question: What lane space is a motorcyclist entitled to?
options: a:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,b:A bicycle lane.,c:Half the lane width.
note: A motorcycle is entitled to the full width of a traffic lane, just like any other motor vehicle. Drivers should not crowd a motorcycle or try to share the same lane side‑by‑side. Giving motorcycles their full lane space improves their ability to maneuver and avoid hazards.

question: Do drivers need to allow the same following distance behind motorcycles as behind cars?
options: a:Yes,b:Only in wet conditions,c:No,d:Only at high speeds
note: You should allow at least the same following distance behind a motorcycle as you would behind a car—and often more. Motorcycles can stop and maneuver quickly, and they are less visible than larger vehicles. Keeping a minimum three‑ to four‑second following distance gives you time to react if the motorcyclist slows or stops suddenly.

question: If a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light and you are turning, who must yield?
options: a:The pedestrian only yields if not in a marked crosswalk.,b:The driver turning must yield to the pedestrian.,c:The first person to move has the right-of-way.,d:The pedestrian must always yield.
note: When you are turning at an intersection, you must yield to pedestrians who are crossing the street you are turning into, whether or not there is a traffic signal or marked crosswalk. Pedestrians in the roadway have the right‑of‑way in crosswalks—marked or unmarked—so you must wait until they have safely crossed before completing your turn.

question: Which of these is NOT part of the searching technique when driving?
options: a:Trying to find your car in a parking lot,b:Checking left,c:Looking ahead and behind for hazards
note: The searching technique in driving means continuously scanning the road ahead, behind, and to the sides for potential hazards. This includes checking left and right at intersections and using your mirrors to monitor traffic. Looking for your parked car in a lot is not part of this hazard‑searching process while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to pass on a two-lane road when your side has a single solid yellow centerline?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: A single solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you must not pass other vehicles. Passing is only allowed when the broken yellow line is on your side, because that indicates you have enough visibility and it is legal to move into the opposing lane when safe.

question: At an intersection, when must you stop for a traffic signal?
options: a:When a green light is flashing,b:At a steady yellow light,c:At a yellow arrow,d:At a flashing red light
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign, and then proceed only when it is safe. Steady yellow, yellow arrows, and flashing green lights generally warn you to prepare to stop or indicate changing right‑of‑way, but they do not always require an immediate stop if you can safely clear the intersection.

question: As a pedestrian, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Waiting for vehicles to stop before stepping out.,b:Wearing reflective clothing at night.,c:Using designated crosswalks.,d:Entering a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
note: Pedestrians must not step into the street or a crosswalk if approaching vehicles are so close that they may not be able to stop in time. Even when you have the right‑of‑way, you should wait until it is clear that drivers see you and can safely stop before you enter the roadway.

question: Is it lawful to use only parking lights while driving at night?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Parking lights alone are not sufficient for driving at night. You must use your headlights from sunset to sunrise and any time visibility is poor so that you can see the road and other drivers can see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than:
options: a:The speed that makes you feel safe.,b:The posted maximum speed only,c:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions.,d:Always at or below 25 mph.
note: You must never drive faster than is reasonable and prudent for current conditions, even if that is below the posted speed limit. Factors like traffic, weather, road surface, and visibility can require you to drive more slowly than the maximum posted speed.

question: How are bicycles classified under traffic law?
options: a:Required to stay on sidewalks,b:Considered vehicles but without the same rights as motor vehicles,c:Considered vehicles and have the same rights as motor vehicles
note: Bicycles are treated as vehicles in traffic law. Cyclists generally have the same rights and duties as drivers of motor vehicles: they may use most roadways, must obey traffic signals and signs, and must yield and signal properly. Some roads (like interstate highways or certain limited-access roads) may prohibit bicycles for safety reasons, but otherwise they are full road users.

question: Is it illegal to use a radar detector in Virginia?
options: a:Only at night,b:No—FALSE,c:Only in commercial vehicles,d:Yes—TRUE
note: In Virginia, it is illegal to use a radar detector in any motor vehicle on public roads. The law prohibits having a radar detector in the vehicle in a condition where it can be used, regardless of time of day or whether the vehicle is commercial or private. Drivers should not rely on radar detectors and must obey posted speed limits at all times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady green light, what should a driver do?
options: a:Continue driving unless pedestrians or vehicles are already in the intersection.,b:Stop if you see a police officer nearby.,c:Treat it as a four-way stop.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if it is safe, but you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection. You should also approach at a speed that allows you to stop safely if the light changes to yellow and then red.

question: When stopped for a violation or equipment check, what documents must a driver produce?
options: a:Only a driver's license.,b:Only proof of insurance.,c:Driver license, registration, and proof of insurance,d:No documents are required to be produced.
note: When an officer stops you for a violation or equipment check, you are generally required to show your driver license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance. Keeping these documents readily accessible helps the stop go smoothly and is part of your legal responsibilities as a driver.

question: If someone is injured in an accident, what should you do?
options: a:Always leave the injured where they are.,b:Avoid moving the injured unless necessary; keep them warm and provide first aid.,c:Move the injured away from the scene immediately.
note: After a crash, do not move an injured person unless there is immediate danger (such as fire, risk of explosion, or oncoming traffic). Unnecessary movement can worsen injuries, especially to the neck or spine. Keep the person warm, reassure them, and provide first aid only if you are trained and it is safe to do so, while you or someone else calls emergency services.

question: What is the risk of eating or drinking while driving?
options: a:It improves reaction time,b:It creates distractions that reduce control and lane-keeping,c:It makes you a better driver because you are not hungry,d:It has no effect
note: Eating or drinking while driving takes at least one hand off the wheel and your attention off the road. This makes it harder to keep your lane position steady and slows your reaction time if traffic suddenly stops or changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill next to a curb, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Keep the rear tires against the curb,b:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb,c:Keep the front tires straight ahead
note: When you park uphill with a curb, you turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will move into the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Low-beam headlights,b:Parking lights,c:High-beam headlights
note: In fog, use low-beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back at you, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and improve visibility without as much glare.

question: How should you treat railroad crossings?
options: a:Dangerous; always look and listen.,b:Safe to cross; trains rarely come.,c:Safe to park near.
note: Railroad crossings are always potential danger zones because trains cannot stop quickly and always have the right-of-way. You should slow, look, and listen for trains, and obey all warning signs, signals, and flaggers before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From the center left-turn lane, which maneuvers are typically allowed?
options: a:You may drive straight through the intersection.,b:You may pass slower vehicles.,c:You may make U-turns only where they are specifically allowed.,d:You may make left turns from either direction.
note: A center left‑turn lane is a shared lane used only for making left turns from either direction, or for permitted U‑turns where allowed by local law. It is not a travel lane and must not be used for passing or driving straight through an intersection.

question: If taking an over-the-counter medication, how should you approach driving?
options: a:Only drive if you feel fine after taking it.,b:Mix it with alcohol to increase effectiveness.,c:Read the label for warnings and ask a doctor or pharmacist if unsure.,d:Assume it has no effect and drive as usual.
note: Many over‑the‑counter medicines can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slowed reaction time. Always read the label for driving or operating‑machinery warnings, and if you are unsure how a medicine might affect you, ask a doctor or pharmacist before driving.

question: When must you stop for a school bus?
options: a:When it approaches you even if its lights are not flashing.,b:If it is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.,c:If you are on an undivided two-lane road and the school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended.
note: On a two‑lane road with no physical divider, you must stop in both directions when a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. Stay stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, even if you do not see children crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Toward the center of the road (left).,b:Toward the curb (right),c:Turn wheels sharply to the left and leave the car in neutral.,d:Keep wheels straight ahead.
note: When parking facing downhill on a two‑way street with a curb, turn your front wheels toward the curb (right). If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will rest against the curb and help prevent it from rolling into traffic.

question: Which behavior helps prevent crashes by improving communication with others?
options: a:Using signals and other cues to communicate intentions.,b:Ignoring other drivers to concentrate on yourself.,c:Driving only on side streets to avoid traffic.,d:Hiding your intentions until the last moment.
note: Crashes are less likely when drivers clearly communicate their intentions. Use turn signals before turning or changing lanes, tap your brake pedal to warn that you are slowing, and use your horn only when necessary to alert others to your presence or a hazard.

question: When you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle, what is required?
options: a:Signal it to pass,b:Ignore it if you are in a hurry,c:Slow down but stay in your lane,d:Drive to the right and stop until it passes
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as far to the right as safely possible and stopping until it has passed. If you are in an intersection, continue through it, then pull over and stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection's traffic signals are out due to a power outage, you should:
options: a:Ignore other vehicles and proceed quickly.,b:Drive through without stopping if you think it's clear.,c:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and proceed when it is your turn.,d:Turn on your hazard lights and continue without stopping.
note: When traffic signals are completely out, you must treat the intersection like a four‑way stop. Come to a complete stop, then proceed in the order of arrival, yielding to any vehicle already in the intersection and to pedestrians. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: Is it legal to drive at night using only your parking lights?
options: a:No — this is unlawful.,b:Yes, it is acceptable everywhere.,c:Only if you are in a well-lit area.,d:Only during emergencies.
note: Parking lights alone are not bright enough for safe night driving and do not meet legal requirements. At night, you must use your headlights so you can see the road and so other drivers can see you. Parking lights are only for when the vehicle is stopped or parked, not moving in traffic.

question: What do round traffic signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:Railroad crossings ahead.,c:School zones.,d:None of the above.
note: In the U.S., round traffic signs are used specifically to warn of a railroad crossing ahead. When you see a round yellow railroad warning sign, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching.

question: If involved in an accident, what are your immediate responsibilities?
options: a:Stop, check for injuries, call for help if needed, and remain at the scene.,b:Leave the scene if no one appears hurt.,c:Move injured people immediately regardless of their condition.,d:Only exchange insurance information and then leave immediately.
note: If you are involved in a collision, you must stop immediately, check for injuries, and call emergency services if needed. Do not leave the scene. Provide reasonable assistance without moving injured persons unless there is immediate danger, and exchange information as required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are you required to signal every time you pull away from a curb?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must signal any time you pull away from a curb or leave a parked position. Signaling lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know that you are about to re‑enter traffic, helping prevent collisions.

question: When you first encounter rain while driving, what is the safe action?
options: a:Increase your following distance but maintain speed,b:Slow down,c:Drive faster to clear the area more quickly
note: When rain first starts, oil and debris on the road mix with water and make the surface very slick. You should slow down, turn on your low‑beam headlights, and increase your following distance so you have more time and space to react. If visibility becomes very poor, safely pull off the road until conditions improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering interstate traffic from an acceleration ramp, who must yield?
options: a:The entering driver has the right-of-way.,b:The driver entering the interstate must yield to drivers already on the interstate.,c:Drivers on the interstate must always slow down.,d:Both must stop before merging
note: Traffic already on the interstate has the right‑of‑way. When using an entrance ramp and acceleration lane, you must adjust your speed to match traffic and yield until there is a safe gap. Do not force your way in or expect other drivers to slow or change lanes for you.

question: If involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what are your immediate responsibilities?
options: a:Only call your insurance company and drive away.,b:Stop and stay at the scene, check for injuries, call 911, and move out of traffic if it is safe to do so.,c:Move victims without checking for injuries first,d:Leave the scene quickly if you are not at fault.
note: If you are involved in a serious crash, you must stop immediately, stay at the scene, and, if possible, move your vehicle out of traffic to a safe place. Check for injuries, call 911 for medical help, and exchange information with other drivers. Do not leave the scene of a crash involving injury, death, or significant property damage.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way,b:Stop immediately where you are without checking surroundings,c:Pull over to the right and stop,d:Turn on hazard lights and continue slowly
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches from behind, you must safely move to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed. Use your mirrors and signals, and do not stop in an intersection. In heavy traffic, continue moving slowly until you can pull to the right and let the vehicle through.

question: Does paying the $500 uninsured motor vehicle fee provide liability insurance coverage?
options: a:Yes,b:No
note: Paying an uninsured motor vehicle fee only allows you to register and operate a vehicle without buying insurance in certain states; it does not provide any liability coverage. If you cause a crash, you are personally responsible for all damages and injuries.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?
options: a:Assume the flagger is not supposed to be there,b:Follow the flagger's directions,c:Do what the surrounding traffic does despite the flagger
note: Flaggers in construction zones are legally authorized to direct traffic. Their instructions have the same authority as traffic signals or signs. Always slow down, be prepared to stop, and follow the flagger’s directions to protect workers and other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up, what should you do?
options: a:Decrease your speed even further,b:Not let other cars pass your vehicle,c:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass
note: If you are driving so slowly that you are blocking or backing up traffic, you must not continue to impede the flow. When it is safe, pull off to the right side of the road or into a turnout and let faster traffic pass, especially on two-lane roads with limited passing opportunities.

question: Before changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Rely only on your mirrors.,b:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.,c:Signal in advance and check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes, signal well in advance, check your mirrors, and then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Mirrors alone do not show vehicles in your blind spots, so the over-the-shoulder check is essential before moving into another lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open (uncontrolled) intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Either driver may proceed without yielding,b:The driver on the left,c:The driver on the right
note: At an open (uncontrolled) intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way and may proceed first when it is safe.

question: When is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:When passing another car.,b:When you have to stop quickly.,c:When you lose control of your car to warn others.
note: Use your horn to warn others of immediate danger, such as when you lose control of your vehicle or another driver is about to collide with you. The horn is a safety device, not for expressing frustration or for routine passing in normal conditions.

question: When other drivers around you are acting angrily, how should you respond?
options: a:Make eye contact to try to calm them,b:React with hand gestures to show you are not intimidated,c:Distance yourself from them and avoid eye contact
note: If another driver is angry or aggressive, do not engage with them. Avoid eye contact and any gestures, and create as much safe space as you can between your vehicle and theirs. This helps prevent the situation from escalating and keeps your focus on driving safely.

question: What is the DMV's vision standard for an unrestricted driver license?
options: a:20/40 or better vision in one or both eyes,b:20/20 or better in one or both eyes,c:20/60 or better vision in one or both eyes
note: For an unrestricted license, you must meet a minimum vision standard so you can see hazards and traffic clearly. A common standard, such as in Virginia, is at least 20/40 vision in one or both eyes with an adequate horizontal field of vision. If your vision is worse than this, you may be restricted or denied a license for safety reasons.

question: When should you use turn signals or hand signals?
options: a:When making turns,b:When changing lanes,c:All of the above,d:When entering or exiting highways
note: Turn or hand signals are required any time you intend to change where your vehicle is going in traffic. Signal before turning, changing lanes, or entering and exiting highways so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know your intentions and can react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp regarding speed?
options: a:Keep your speed constant on the ramp,b:Slow down before you enter the exit ramp,c:Slow down once you have moved onto the exit ramp
note: You should adjust your speed before you reach the exit ramp so you can leave the freeway smoothly and under control. Signal and move into the exit lane early, then slow down to a safe speed before entering the ramp, and continue adjusting to any posted or advisory ramp speed as you proceed.

question: What should drivers know about large trucks?
options: a:They are easier to overtake in curves,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles,c:They have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop,d:They need less space to turn
note: Large trucks are heavier and longer than passenger vehicles, so they need more distance to stop and more room to turn and maneuver. They also have large blind spots along the sides, rear, and sometimes in front. Avoid driving in these blind spots and give trucks extra space when passing or when they are turning.

question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep tires properly inflated and with good tread,b:Drive with cruise control on,c:Use underinflated tires to increase traction.,d:Increase speed in heavy rain.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water instead of gripping the road. You reduce this risk by keeping your tires properly inflated, maintaining good tread depth, and slowing down in wet conditions. Options that involve speeding up, using cruise control, or underinflating tires all increase the chance of losing traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic light turns yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Begin slowing and be prepared to stop if it is safe to do so.,c:Stop abruptly in the center of the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. If you can stop safely before the intersection, you should slow down and prepare to stop. You should not speed up to beat the red, and you should not stop abruptly in the middle of the intersection; if you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through with caution.

question: On slippery roads, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed and avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.,b:Always drive at the posted maximum speed.,c:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less grip, so it is easier to skid. You should reduce your speed, increase following distance, and avoid sudden braking, acceleration, or sharp steering. Cruise control should not be used on slippery surfaces because it can cause the vehicle to accelerate or maintain speed when you actually need to slow down gently.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road with opposing traffic, when should you return to the driving lane?
options: a:When you reach the next mile marker,b:When there is enough room between you and the vehicle passed.,c:Only after the passed vehicle signals.,d:Immediately after passing regardless of distance.
note: When passing, you must not move back into your lane until there is a safe gap between you and the vehicle you passed. A good rule is to wait until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, then signal and return smoothly. Cutting back too soon can force the other driver to brake and creates a collision risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What best ensures safety when you are about to back your vehicle?
options: a:Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse,b:Check your rearview mirrors only,c:Check behind the vehicle on foot before getting into the driver's seat
note: Before backing, the safest practice is to walk behind your vehicle and check for children, pets, or objects you cannot see from the driver’s seat. After that, back up slowly while using your mirrors and any backup camera, and continue to look over your shoulder. Relying only on mirrors or just honking the horn does not ensure the area behind you is clear.

question: Where should you try to keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
