options: a:On all sides of your vehicle.,b:Only behind your vehicle.,c:Only in front of the vehicle.,d:Only to the left and right of your vehicle
note: You should always try to keep a space cushion on all sides of your vehicle. Extra space in front, behind, and to the sides gives you time and room to react, brake, or steer away from hazards without sudden or unsafe maneuvers.

question: What typically causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Sudden stops.,b:Old windshield wipers,c:Excessive stops.,d:Driving too fast for wet road conditions so tires cannot clear water.
note: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads and your tires ride up on a thin layer of water instead of gripping the pavement. When this occurs, you can lose steering and braking control. Slowing down in wet conditions and having good tire tread helps prevent hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when approaching a steady yellow traffic light?
options: a:Accelerate to beat the red light.,b:Assume you have right-of-way and continue.,c:Slow to a stop unless you are already in the intersection.,d:Stop abruptly in the lane
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through and clear the intersection; do not speed up to beat the red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where are U-turns allowed in business districts, cities, and towns?
options: a:Anywhere on the roadway,b:Only in parking lots,c:Only on highways,d:Generally only at intersections in business districts, where not otherwise prohibited by signs or local law
note: In many states, U‑turns in business districts are only allowed at intersections unless signs prohibit them. You must always check for signs, traffic, and enough visibility and space to complete the turn safely. Never make a U‑turn mid‑block in a business district where it is generally not permitted.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Increase speed to clear the tracks,b:Slow down, look for trains, and be ready to stop,c:Drive across without stopping if you do not see a train,d:Sound your horn and proceed
note: When approaching a railroad crossing, slow down and look carefully in both directions for trains. Be prepared to stop if a train is approaching or warning devices are active. Never try to beat a train across the tracks; trains are much faster and closer than they may appear.

question: Under what circumstances can DMV deny or suspend driving privileges for persons under 18?
options: a:If the juvenile misses school occasionally.,b:If the juvenile is under 21,c:If the juvenile is found delinquent by a court or involved in alcohol/drug-related offenses.,d:If the juvenile lacks parental supervision but has no offenses.
note: DMVs can deny or suspend the driving privileges of minors who are adjudicated delinquent by a court, or who are involved in alcohol- or drug-related offenses or certain serious traffic violations. These actions are tied to behavior and legal findings, not simply age, occasional school absences, or lack of parental supervision.

question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When the other driver signals you to return,b:When the entire passed vehicle is visible in your rearview mirror,c:When you feel it is safe,d:When your front bumper aligns with the other's rear bumper
note: After passing, you should not move back into your original lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead and reduces the risk of cutting off the other driver or causing a rear-end collision.

question: Regulatory signs are usually what color and must always be obeyed?
options: a:Yellow,b:White (many regulatory signs are white with black lettering, though some regulatory signs use other colors such as red),c:Blue,d:Green
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do, such as speed limits, lane use, and parking rules. Many regulatory signs are white with black lettering or symbols, but some important regulatory signs use other colors, such as red (STOP, YIELD, DO NOT ENTER, WRONG WAY) or black/white/red combinations. Regardless of color variation, regulatory signs are legally enforceable and must always be obeyed.

question: How does increasing your speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It makes peripheral vision better,b:It increases your field of vision,c:It decreases your field of vision,d:It has no effect
note: As your speed increases, your field of vision effectively narrows. You see less to the sides and tend to focus more straight ahead, which makes it easier to miss hazards entering from the sides. This is why high speeds require extra caution and scanning.

question: What do pentagonal road signs indicate?
options: a:Railroad crossings,b:Speed limits,c:School zones and school crossings,d:No passing zones
note: Pentagonal (five-sided) signs are used for school zones and school crossings. They alert you to slow down, watch for children, and obey any posted speed limits or crossing guards in the area.

question: Which of the following about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You may always go around gates if no train is visible.,b:All crossings have flashing signals and gates.,c:It is illegal to go around lowered gates,d:You never have to stop at a crossing directed by a flagger.
note: At railroad crossings, you must never drive around or under lowered gates, even if you do not see a train. Some crossings do not have lights or gates, so you must look and listen carefully. If a flagger is present, you must obey their directions just as you would a traffic signal or police officer.

question: Should you use high beams when driving in fog?
options: a:No, use low beams or fog lights in fog.,b:Use parking lights instead of headlights in fog.,c:Use high beams only if there are no other vehicles.,d:Yes, high beams help you see better in fog.
note: In fog, you should not use high beams because the light reflects off the water droplets and shines back at you, making it harder to see. Use low-beam headlights or fog lights so you can see the road and be seen by others without creating glare.

question: Why is it important to be alert to motorcycles?
options: a:They are smaller and harder to see than cars,b:They rarely use headlights,c:Motorcyclists are less skilled,d:They always drive at the speed limit
note: Motorcycles are much smaller than cars and can be hidden easily in blind spots or behind other vehicles. Because they are harder to see and their speed and distance can be difficult to judge, you must look carefully for them, especially when changing lanes or turning.

question: What do your brake lights signal to drivers behind you?
options: a:You are making a turn.,b:You are slowing down or stopping.,c:You have your emergency brake on.,d:You are driving with your headlights on.
note: Brake lights warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping so they have time to react and avoid a rear-end collision. Keeping your brake lights in good working order is an important part of safe driving.

question: Anything that causes you to ____ can lead to a crash.
options: a:Check mirrors regularly.,b:Drive at the posted speed limit.,c:Use your turn signal.,d:Take your attention away from driving.
note: Anything that takes your attention away from driving—such as using a phone, eating, or looking away from the road—can increase your risk of a crash. Safe drivers stay focused on the road, keep their hands on the wheel, and avoid distractions.

question: What is the most important rule for managing speed when approaching a curve?
options: a:Accelerate gently as you enter the curve,b:Slow down before you enter the curve,c:Drive at the posted speed as you enter then brake at the sharpest part
note: Slow down before entering a curve so you can steer smoothly and keep traction. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause skidding or loss of control because your tires are already working to turn the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when turning or changing lanes?
options: a:Always signal your intentions,b:Signal only on highways,c:Signal only at night.,d:Signal only when other traffic is present.
note: You must always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb, even if you do not see other traffic. Signaling every time makes your actions predictable and helps prevent crashes.

question: When a transit bus signals to merge back into traffic after stopping, you must:
options: a:Yield to allow the bus to re-enter safely.,b:Speed up to pass the bus before it merges.,c:Ignore the bus's signal and maintain speed.,d:Honk to alert the driver.
note: When a transit bus signals that it is pulling out from a stop, you should yield and allow it to re-enter traffic when it is safe. Slowing, changing lanes, or briefly stopping gives the large vehicle enough space to merge safely.

question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Exercise to sweat it out.,b:Allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol.,c:Drink coffee and rest.
note: The only effective way to reduce BAC is to allow your body time to metabolize the alcohol; coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not reduce BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is a prohibited passing situation?
options: a:All of the above,b:When a school bus is stopped to load/unload on a public road without a physical barrier,c:When a solid line marks the left side of your lane,d:When passing requires leaving the paved roadway
note: You must not pass when a solid line is on your side of the center, when a school bus is stopped to load or unload children on an undivided road, or when passing would require leaving the paved roadway. All of these situations are unsafe or illegal, so they are all prohibited.

question: When parking next to a curb, what is the maximum distance from the curb you may park?
options: a:18 inches,b:12 inches (one foot),c:2 feet,d:6 inches
note: On most U.S. roads where curb parking is allowed, you must park close and parallel to the curb, generally within one foot (12 inches). Parking farther out can block traffic and create a hazard, so always pull in as close as safely possible without scraping the curb.

question: To avoid driving unsafely due to health or medication, you should:
options: a:Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.,b:Drive within your physical limitations.,c:Ignore medicine warnings if you feel fine.
note: To avoid unsafe driving due to health or medication, you should both maintain your health and understand how any medical conditions or medicines affect your driving. Regular physical exams and staying physically fit help ensure you are medically able to drive safely and recognize when you should not drive or should limit your driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a steady red traffic light, what must you do?
options: a:Continue through if no other traffic is present,b:Slow down and proceed with caution,c:Come to a complete stop
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, before the crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. After stopping, you may turn right (and sometimes left from a one-way to a one-way) if there is no sign prohibiting it and the way is clear, but the required first action is always a full stop.

question: If you intend to move from the right lane to the left on a multilane highway, what should you check?
options: a:Sound your horn and change lanes quickly,b:Only check the rearview mirror.,c:Look over your left shoulder to check the blind spot,d:Turn on your signal and immediately change lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. This over-the-shoulder glance lets you see vehicles that do not appear in your mirrors and helps you change lanes safely.

question: Which headlights should you use in the rain?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Emergency flashers.,d:Low beam headlights.
note: In rain, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off rain, fog, or snow and create glare, making it harder for you to see and for others to see you. Low beams provide better visibility and help other drivers notice your vehicle.

question: If railroad crossing signals are flashing as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed cautiously without stopping.,b:Stop well back (no closer than 15 feet) and wait for the train to pass.,c:Drive around lowered gates if no train is visible.,d:Slow down and cross quickly before the train arrives.
note: When railroad crossing lights are flashing or gates are down, you must stop at least 15 feet from the tracks and wait until the train has passed and the signals stop before crossing. Never drive around lowered gates or try to beat a train; trains cannot stop quickly and always have the right of way.

question: If a fire engine is following you on a two-lane street but is not using its emergency lights or siren, how should you respond?
options: a:Speed up to get out of its way,b:Stop as quickly as possible,c:Continue driving in a normal manner
note: You are only required to yield and pull over for emergency vehicles when they are using their lights and/or siren. If a fire engine is behind you without emergency signals activated, treat it like any other vehicle and continue driving normally, obeying all traffic laws.

question: What is the shape of a stop sign?
options: a:Octagon,b:Circle,c:Diamond,d:Rectangle
note: A stop sign is an octagon, meaning it has eight sides. This unique shape helps drivers recognize it quickly, even in poor visibility or if the sign is partially blocked, so they know a complete stop is required.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Open your window to stay alert,b:Get some coffee and keep going,c:Stop driving and rest
note: If you feel tired while driving, you should stop driving and rest or change drivers. Fatigue slows your reaction time and affects judgment much like alcohol, and tricks like opening a window or drinking coffee do not make you safe enough to continue for long.

question: Must you use headlights whenever you use windshield wipers because of weather?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Many states, including Virginia, require you to use headlights whenever your windshield wipers are in use due to rain, snow, or other weather. This law helps other drivers see you better in reduced-visibility conditions. Even in states without this specific rule, turning on headlights with wipers is a recommended safety practice.

question: How serious is drinking alcohol and driving?
options: a:A serious traffic safety problem.,b:Not a problem for experienced drivers,c:A minor traffic issue.,d:Safe if you have had only a few drinks.
note: Alcohol and many drugs slow your reaction time, reduce coordination, and affect judgment, making it much harder to see hazards and respond in time. Because this greatly increases crash risk and can cause serious injury or death, drinking and driving is considered a very serious traffic safety problem.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an uncontrolled intersection, what is the correct action?
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed without checking,b:Yield to all other drivers regardless of their position,c:Stop,d:Slow down, look carefully in all directions, and be prepared to yield to traffic and pedestrians already in or approaching the intersection.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), you are not required to stop every time, but you must approach with caution. Slow down, scan left-right-left, and be prepared to yield. Yield to any vehicle already in the intersection and to vehicles on your right if you arrive at the same time. Stop only if needed for safety or to yield the right-of-way.

question: Which statement about changing weather and driving is correct?
options: a:Ignore vehicles behind you in bad weather.,b:A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.,c:Always increase your speed in rain.
note: When weather changes suddenly—such as rain, fog, snow, or strong wind—you must adjust how you drive. This usually means slowing down, increasing following distance, turning on appropriate lights, and being especially alert to other vehicles, including those behind you. You should never speed up just because of bad weather.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is trying to pass your car, how should you respond?
options: a:Signal them when it is safe for them to pass.,b:Pull off the road immediately.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing,d:Stay in your lane and maintain or slightly reduce your speed to allow the other driver to pass safely.
note: When another driver is passing you, stay in your lane and maintain a steady speed or slightly reduce speed to help them pass safely. Do not speed up or signal them when to pass. You should focus on keeping your vehicle predictable and allowing enough space and time for the passing vehicle to complete the maneuver safely.

question: If children are playing near your driveway and you need to back out, what should you do before moving?
options: a:Get out and walk to the rear of the car to ensure the way is clear,b:Back out slowly relying on mirrors only,c:Sound your horn to warn them,d:Rev your engine to alert them
note: Children can be hard to see behind a vehicle, and mirrors or cameras may not show them clearly. Before backing out of a driveway where children are playing, walk to the rear of the vehicle and check the area directly behind and around it. Once you know it is clear, back out slowly and continue checking around you.

question: Which steps should you take when changing lanes on a highway?
options: a:Rely solely on your mirrors,b:Signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder before changing lanes,c:Only signal and change lanes quickly,d:Only change lanes if other drivers wave you
note: When changing lanes, always signal, check your mirrors, and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving. Never rely only on mirrors or on other drivers waving you through.

question: When driving on wet pavement, what should you remember?
options: a:Give extra stopping distance,b:Pavement is especially slippery just after it starts raining,c:Wet roads can cause hydroplaning,d:All of the above
note: On wet pavement, you need more distance to stop, the road is especially slippery right after rain begins, and water buildup can cause hydroplaning where your tires lose contact with the road. Because all of these are true, you should slow down and increase following distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with lights flashing, you must:
options: a:Drive to the right and stop.,b:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane.,c:Slow down and change lanes away from it if possible.
note: When approaching a stopped emergency, tow, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes away if safe; otherwise slow down and give space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street, which lane should you begin from?
options: a:The left lane,b:The middle lane,c:The right lane,d:Any lane works
note: On a one‑way street with multiple lanes, you must begin a left turn from the leftmost lane that is legal for travel. This keeps you out of the path of through traffic and lines you up correctly for the turn.

question: Is it true that drivers should avoid staying beside large vehicles for long periods because of their blind spots?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots along both sides, as well as in front and behind. If you linger next to them, the driver may not see you. Pass promptly and safely, and avoid driving alongside large vehicles for long periods.

question: What is the most common mistake drivers make when backing?
options: a:False — mirrors and cameras alone are not sufficient.,b:False — relying on a backup camera only is unsafe.,c:True — failing to look both ways behind them is a common mistake.
note: When backing, you must turn your head and look through the rear window in both directions, not just rely on mirrors or cameras. Mirrors and backup cameras have blind spots and may not show small children, pedestrians, or objects close to your vehicle. Physically looking over your shoulder gives you the widest, clearest view and helps prevent collisions while reversing.

question: Does a 'Merging lanes' sign mean drivers should be prepared to change lanes or allow others to merge?
options: a:False,b:True
note: A merging lanes sign warns that two traffic lanes will come together. Drivers in both lanes should be prepared to adjust speed, change lanes if needed, or create space so vehicles can merge safely. You should not speed up to block others; instead, cooperate so traffic can blend smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which actions should you take before changing lanes?
options: a:Check your blind spot only,b:Signal only,c:Signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder
note: Before changing lanes, you should signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Signaling alone is not enough, and checking only the blind spot without signaling or using mirrors is also unsafe. All three steps together help ensure the lane is clear and that other drivers know your intentions.

question: Which of the following summarizes your responsibilities each time you drive?
options: a:Assume others will always yield to you.,b:Ignore traffic laws if roads are empty.,c:Accept responsibility for your actions and obey Virginia traffic laws.,d:Drive only when accompanied.
note: Each time you drive, you are responsible for following all traffic laws, controlling your vehicle safely, and helping protect other road users. You cannot assume others will always yield or behave correctly, so you must drive defensively, obey the law, and be prepared for the unexpected.

question: When must you remain stopped for a school bus with flashing signals and the stop arm extended?
options: a:Until the bus driver waves you by.,b:Only if you are driving in the same direction as the bus.,c:Until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,d:Until all children are clear of the roadway and the bus moves again.
note: When a school bus has red flashing lights and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Children may still be near the bus or about to cross even if you do not see them. Do not move again until the bus’s signals are turned off, unless your state provides a specific divided-highway exception.

question: Which of the following does NOT normally occur after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down,b:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted,c:You are more alert
note: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your reflexes and reaction time, reduces alertness, and distorts your judgment of speed, distance, and risk. Feeling or becoming more alert is not a normal effect of drinking, so that choice is the one that does not occur.

question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road means:
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,b:Do not change lanes under any circumstances.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and you may change lanes when safe.,d:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and you may pass.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a single broken white line when it is safe to change lanes or pass. Solid yellow or white lines are used where passing or lane changes are restricted.

question: What driving habit can help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Accelerating quickly from stops,b:Idling in driveways with the engine running,c:Frequent hard braking,d:Slowing down gradually and avoiding sudden stops
note: Smooth, gradual driving uses less fuel. Looking ahead, easing off the accelerator early, and slowing down gradually avoids hard braking and repeated rapid acceleration, which both waste gasoline.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are without moving,b:Speed up to get out of the way,c:Drive slowly and let it pass on your left,d:Drive as far to the right as possible and stop
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as you can and stopping until it has passed, unless otherwise directed by law enforcement.

question: Combining alcohol with drugs can cause what effect?
options: a:Prevent impairment entirely,b:Increase the effects of both substances,c:Have no interaction,d:Reduce the effects making them safe
note: Alcohol and many drugs have a compounding effect: when taken together, they can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment more than either substance alone. This makes driving far more dangerous.

question: What is the 'No zone' in relation to trucks and buses?
options: a:Blind spots around a truck or bus where the vehicle cannot see you.,b:A quiet zone near schools,c:A restricted parking zone.,d:A speed enforcement area for trucks.
note: The No-Zone is the large blind-spot area around trucks and buses where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Staying out of these areas, especially along the sides, directly behind, and close in front of large vehicles, helps prevent collisions because the truck or bus driver may not know you are there.

question: When children are playing nearby, what should you expect them to do?
options: a:Always know when it is safe to cross.,b:Stop at the curb before crossing.,c:Obey crossing guards reliably,d:Run into the street without looking.
note: Children near the road are unpredictable and may suddenly run into the street without looking. When you see children playing, slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop quickly because they may not understand traffic dangers or follow safety rules.

question: What is the safest location to install a child safety seat in a car?
options: a:The center of the back seat,b:The front passenger seat,c:The driver's side back seat,d:Any seat with an airbag
note: The center of the rear seat is generally the safest place for a child safety seat because it is farthest from potential impact points in most crashes and away from side airbags. Always install the seat according to the vehicle and seat manufacturer’s instructions, and never place a rear‑facing child seat in front of an active airbag.

question: When driving near light rail vehicles, which precaution should you always take?
options: a:Ignore posted signs if no train is visible,b:Assume you have the right-of-way at all crossings,c:Expect trains on any track at any time,d:Drive alongside the train in its lane to keep traffic moving
note: Light rail vehicles are large, fast, and need a long distance to stop. Always expect a train on any track at any time, obey all signals and signs, and never stop on the tracks. Cross only when you are sure you can clear the tracks completely without stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, who yields?
options: a:The car on the left shall yield to the car on the right.,b:The car on the right shall yield to the car on the left.,c:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,d:The faster vehicle has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals controlling the intersection.

question: About how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer be able to travel before stopping from 55 mph?
options: a:400 feet.,b:50 feet,c:125 feet
note: A fully loaded tractor‑trailer needs much more distance to stop than a passenger car. At 55 mph, it can take close to 400 feet from the moment the driver reacts until the truck comes to a complete stop. This is why you should never cut closely in front of large trucks and should allow them extra space.

question: When stopping on an uphill slope, when should you increase your space cushion?
options: a:On an uphill slope.,b:At an intersection.,c:At a stop sign.
note: When you are stopped on an uphill slope, leave extra space between you and the vehicle ahead. When traffic starts moving, the vehicle in front of you may roll backward slightly before moving forward, especially if it has a manual transmission. A larger space cushion helps prevent a rear‑end collision.

question: Which actions can lead to your license being revoked or suspended?
options: a:Making a false statement to the DMV.,b:Driving with a broken taillight.,c:Running out of fuel on the highway.,d:Parking in a no-parking zone
note: Making a false statement to the DMV is considered fraud and can result in your license being suspended or revoked. Serious violations such as driving under the influence, failing to appear in court, or committing certain crimes related to driving can also lead to loss of driving privileges.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal, what should you do?
options: a:Honk to make them move,b:Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely,c:Speed up to pass in front of them,d:Proceed because you have the right-of-way
note: Even if you have a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the crosswalk, including those crossing against the signal. Slow or stop as needed and allow them to cross safely before you proceed. This reduces the risk of hitting a pedestrian and is required by law in most situations.

question: Do large vehicles have blind spots that can extend far behind them?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots, called "no‑zones," along the sides and directly behind them. The area behind a large vehicle can extend a long distance where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. If you follow too closely, the driver may not know you are there, so always leave extra following distance.

question: What happens if you take drugs along with alcohol?
options: a:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,b:It lessens the effect of alcohol.,c:It neutralizes alcohol impairment,d:It increases the risk of causing a crash.
note: Combining alcohol with any drugs or medications greatly increases impairment. The substances can interact and intensify each other’s effects, slowing your reaction time, harming judgment, and making it much more likely you will cause a crash.

question: What are the consequences of driving in Virginia without liability insurance?
options: a:A small warning with no financial penalty.,b:Only higher premiums later.,c:Suspension of your driving and vehicle registration privileges and a $500 fee until you provide proof of insurance.,d:No consequences if you pay later
note: In Virginia, you must either carry the required liability insurance or pay the uninsured motor vehicle fee. If you are caught driving without meeting one of these requirements, your driving and vehicle registration privileges can be suspended. To restore them, you must pay a $500 fee, provide proof of insurance (SR-22), and meet any reinstatement requirements.

question: How should you treat a railroad crossbuck sign?
options: a:As an advisory only that you may ignore if no train is visible.,b:As a pedestrian-only crossing sign,c:As a stop sign always.,d:Like a yield sign — yield to any oncoming trains.
note: A railroad crossbuck marks the location of a railroad crossing and functions like a yield sign. You must slow, look, and listen for trains, and yield the right-of-way to any approaching train. Never cross if a train is coming or if warning devices are active.

question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:Never — emergency vehicles must avoid you.,b:Only if a police officer tells you to do so.,c:When you see flashing lights or hear a siren.,d:Only if they are behind you.
note: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren from an emergency vehicle, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless otherwise directed by a police officer.

question: What is the most effective action to lower your risk of injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Drive only on weekdays.,b:Stay in the right lane on highways.,c:Keep windows open,d:Wear your seat belt.
note: Wearing your seat belt every time you drive is the single most effective way to reduce your risk of serious injury or death in a crash. Seat belts keep you inside the vehicle, spread crash forces over stronger parts of your body, and work together with airbags for maximum protection.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage (beer, wine, mixed drinks) change how alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you most,b:Different beverage types have the same effect; only the amount matters,c:Beer affects you less than wine
note: Alcohol affects your brain and body based on how much pure alcohol (ethanol) you consume and how quickly it enters your bloodstream, not on whether it comes from beer, wine, or mixed drinks. A standard drink of beer, wine, or liquor contains about the same amount of alcohol, so any type can equally impair reflexes and judgment if the total alcohol amount is the same.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicates you should:
options: a:Do not pass.,b:Pass with caution.,c:Slow down.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you must not pass vehicles ahead of you because it is unsafe to move into the oncoming lane. You may still turn left into driveways or side roads where allowed, but you cannot cross that line to pass another vehicle.

question: Is increasing your vehicle's speed the best way to avoid loss of control in wet conditions?
options: a:False,b:True
note: On wet roads, higher speeds increase the risk of hydroplaning, where your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. To maintain control, you should slow down, avoid sudden steering or braking, and drive smoothly. Speeding up in wet conditions makes loss of control more likely, not less.

question: When an emergency vehicle is using its siren and lights, drivers must:
options: a:Accelerate to clear the area immediately.,b:Continue at the same speed and ignore the vehicle.,c:Stop in the travel lane and wait for it to pass.,d:Yield the right-of-way and follow any loudspeaker instructions.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using its siren and flashing lights, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop if possible, and follow any instructions given over a loudspeaker. Do not speed up, block, or try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

question: Is it lawful to drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other motor vehicle. You must not drive side-by-side with a motorcycle in the same lane because it reduces the motorcyclist’s space to maneuver and react to hazards. Always give motorcycles a full lane and extra following distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a “Merging traffic” sign on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Always remain at your present speed,b:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them,c:Make room for entering vehicles and move over a lane if safe
note: A merging traffic sign warns that vehicles will be entering your lane. You should be prepared to adjust your speed and, if it is safe, move over a lane to create space. Making room helps traffic flow smoothly and reduces the risk of collisions at the merge point.

question: How can you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder to the side you intend to move into.,b:Use only the outside mirror on the same side.,c:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,d:Trust lane-assist systems without looking
note: Mirrors do not show the areas directly alongside your vehicle, called blind spots. Before changing lanes, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This head check, combined with mirror use and signaling, helps ensure the lane is clear.

question: When it starts to sleet or snow while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off windshield wipers to avoid streaks,b:Speed up to get through the area faster,c:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and increase following distance,d:Keep normal following distance
note: In sleet or snow, roads become slippery and stopping distances increase. Keep your windshield, windows, and mirrors clear for maximum visibility, slow down, and increase your following distance so you have more time and space to react if traffic ahead slows or stops.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, what should drivers do?
options: a:Slow down and pass on the right,b:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, then proceed only when it is clearly safe.,c:Honk before passing on the left.,d:Pass cautiously if you think children are done.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing, the stop arm is withdrawn, and it is clearly safe to proceed. On undivided roads, traffic in both directions must stop; on divided highways, only traffic traveling in the same direction as the bus must stop.

question: Which of these can be a sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Weaving between lanes,b:All of the above,c:Driving more slowly than traffic,d:Making quick and sudden stops
note: Impaired drivers often show several warning signs, such as weaving or drifting between lanes, driving noticeably slower or faster than surrounding traffic, and making sudden or jerky stops. Any of these behaviors can indicate a drunk or impaired driver, so you should increase your distance and avoid engaging with them.

question: Should you use low-beam headlights when driving in fog?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off water droplets in the fog and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light lower and reduce reflection, improving your ability to see the road and be seen by others.

question: A downward-pointing triangular traffic sign generally means:
options: a:School zone ahead.,b:No passing zone.,c:Construction ahead.,d:Yield — give way to other traffic.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is the standard shape for a yield sign. When you see this sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary to let other traffic, bicycles, or pedestrians go first.

question: Where are stop lines painted on the roadway?
options: a:On hills and curves,b:At highway exits only,c:Next to churches and schools,d:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across lanes at intersections and before pedestrian crosswalks. They show where you must stop at a stop sign or red light so that you stay clear of crosswalks and intersecting traffic.

question: When an emergency vehicle displays flashing red or blue lights, what should you do?
options: a:Pull over to the side and stop,b:Yell at the driver to pass,c:Continue driving but stay out of its way,d:Try to finish your trip before stopping
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights and/or a siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
options: a:Only a recommended speed,b:The exact speed you must travel to avoid a ticket,c:The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed under ideal conditions, not a target speed. You must drive slower when road, traffic, or weather conditions make the posted speed unsafe, and you can be cited for driving too fast for conditions even if you are below the limit.

question: When are you required to have your headlights on?
options: a:Whenever you use your windshield wipers due to weather.,b:Only in clear daylight.,c:Only at sunset.
note: Headlights are required from sunset to sunrise and any time visibility is reduced by weather. Many states also require headlights whenever windshield wipers are in continuous use due to rain, snow, or other precipitation so other drivers can see you more easily.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal indicate?
options: a:The protected turning movement is ending and you should prepare to stop.,b:You may turn without yielding under any circumstances.,c:No turning is permitted for any vehicles.,d:The signal is malfunctioning.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning phase is ending. You should prepare to stop if it is safe to do so, or complete the turn if you are already in the intersection, and be ready to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when the signal changes.

question: Which of these is a common cause of distracted driving?
options: a:Changing a radio station or CD.,b:Eating.,c:Talking or texting on a cellular phone.,d:All of the above.
note: Distracted driving has three main types: visual (eyes off the road), manual (hands off the wheel), and cognitive (mind off driving). Changing the radio, eating, and using a phone (talking or texting) are all common distractions that can lead to crashes, so they should all be avoided while driving.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It improves fuel efficiency.,b:It only causes minor noise issues.,c:It can allow carbon monoxide into the passenger compartment and cause poisoning.,d:It increases tire wear.
note: A leaky exhaust system can let carbon monoxide and other exhaust gases enter the passenger area. Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless and can quickly cause headache, dizziness, unconsciousness, and even death, so exhaust leaks must be repaired immediately.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey indicated instructions are called what?
options: a:Warning signs,b:Information signs,c:Regulatory signs
note: Regulatory signs tell you about traffic laws and rules you must follow, such as speed limits, stop, yield, and no-turn signs. Ignoring regulatory signs is a traffic violation and can lead to crashes and citations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When visibility is reduced to 500 feet or less due to fog, what must you do about headlights?
options: a:Use only parking lights,b:Use low beam headlights,c:Drive without headlights,d:Use high beam headlights
note: Use low beam headlights (or fog lights if your vehicle has them) whenever visibility is seriously reduced, such as in fog, heavy rain, or snow. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can create glare, making it even harder to see. Parking lights alone are not sufficient for being seen by other drivers.

question: If a solid white edge line on the right slants left toward the center, what does that indicate?
options: a:A passing zone begins,b:There is an intersection ahead,c:The road narrows ahead,d:You must turn left ahead
note: A solid white edge line marks the right edge of the roadway. When this line angles or slants toward the center of the road, it is warning you that the usable roadway is getting narrower ahead, so you should be prepared to adjust your position and speed.

question: What does an octagonal road sign always indicate?
options: a:Stop.,b:Speed limit.,c:Yield.,d:Hospital ahead
note: An octagonal (eight‑sided) sign is used only for STOP signs in the United States. When you see this shape, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Which actions reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Do not speed on wet roads.,b:Ignore tire tread wear.,c:Drive faster to reduce contact time with water.,d:Use cruise control in heavy rain
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water instead of the road surface, causing a loss of traction and steering control. Driving more slowly on wet roads, along with having good tire tread and proper inflation, greatly reduces the risk of hydroplaning. Speeding, worn tires, and using cruise control in heavy rain all increase the risk.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Lightly tap the brake pedal.,b:Hold down the brake pedal.,c:Firmly pump your brakes.
note: In a vehicle without ABS, you should use a firm pumping action on the brake pedal in an emergency stop. This helps prevent the wheels from locking up so you can maintain some steering control. Holding the pedal down hard in a non‑ABS car can cause the wheels to lock and the vehicle to skid.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?
options: a:Yes,b:No,c:Only if there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Crossing double solid yellow lines to pass is prohibited; you may only cross to make a permitted left turn into or from a driveway or alley.

question: Because motorcycles are smaller, what should you do when pulling out into traffic?
options: a:Never drive in a motorcyclist's lane,b:Use extra caution before pulling out in front of a motorcycle,c:Always try to share a lane with a motorcycle
note: Motorcycles are smaller and can be harder to see and judge for speed and distance. Before pulling out into traffic, look carefully for motorcycles, check mirrors and blind spots, and allow extra time and space before entering their path. Never try to share the same lane side‑by‑side with a motorcycle; they are entitled to a full lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the center of the road has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is on your side, when may you pass?
options: a:Only on expressways.,b:When traffic is clear.,c:Only in an emergency.,d:Never
note: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means only the side with the broken line may pass. If the broken line is on your side, you may cross it to pass another vehicle, but only when you have enough clear distance, there is no oncoming traffic, and it is otherwise safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway with double solid yellow lines, you may:
options: a:Never cross to pass slower traffic.,b:Cross to pass slower traffic when no oncoming traffic is present.,c:Cross only to make a left turn into or from a driveway, side road, or alley
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and prohibit passing for both directions. You must not cross them to pass another vehicle. You may, however, cross double solid yellow lines to make a permitted left turn into or from a driveway, side road, or alley when it is safe.

question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, what should you do beforehand?
options: a:Plan your route in advance,b:Only bring a cell phone,c:Drive without preparation,d:Rely only on road signs
note: Before driving in an unfamiliar area, plan your route in advance using a map, GPS, or written directions. Knowing your route ahead of time reduces the need to look at devices or signs while driving, which helps you stay focused on the road and avoid last‑minute maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.,b:Stop and make a U-turn on the highway.,c:Signal and reverse to the exit,d:Get off at the next exit and return to the missed exit.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, keep driving to the next exit. Never stop, back up, or make a U-turn on the highway or shoulder, because traffic is moving at high speed and drivers do not expect a vehicle going backward or turning around. Exit safely at the next opportunity, then re-enter the highway and return to the exit you missed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is a situation where you should not attempt to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When traffic is heavy and there is no safe opening to move into another lane.,b:On a hill or curve where you cannot see far enough ahead.,c:When passing on a freeway with multiple lanes and you can safely change lanes.
note: You must not pass when your view of oncoming traffic is blocked, such as on a hill or a curve, because you cannot be sure the opposite lane is clear for the distance you need. Passing is also prohibited in other no‑passing zones, like near intersections, railroad crossings, and where there are solid center lines or posted no‑passing signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane road, you should not attempt to pass unless you can:
options: a:Cross double solid lines to pass.,b:Pass as quickly as possible regardless of visibility.,c:Clearly see the road ahead and return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,d:Honk continuously while passing.
note: On a two‑way, two‑lane road, only pass when you can clearly see far enough ahead, there are no oncoming vehicles close to you, and you can complete the pass and return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic. You must also make sure passing is legal—there should be a dashed center line on your side and no signs or markings prohibiting passing.

question: Who should wear seat belts for maximum effectiveness?
options: a:All occupants of the vehicle,b:The person driving the car only,c:Passengers only on long trips
note: For maximum protection, everyone in the vehicle should use a seat belt or appropriate child restraint on every trip, no matter how short. Lap and shoulder belts greatly reduce the risk of serious injury or death in a crash by keeping occupants from being thrown forward or ejected.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a dashed white line on the highway?
options: a:Only when passing is illegal.,b:When it is safe to change lanes.,c:Only during daytime hours.,d:Never.
note: A dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors, signaling, and making sure there is enough space in the lane you are entering.

question: Why must you be careful when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Bicycles always have the right-of-way.,b:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.,c:You will always be fined for passing too closely.,d:Bicyclists should ride on sidewalks only.
note: On two‑lane roads, you must move partly or fully into the oncoming lane to pass a bicycle. Oncoming drivers may not expect this and might not see you in time, so you must check carefully for oncoming traffic and only pass when you have enough clear distance and can do so without forcing anyone to brake or swerve.

question: What do work zone signs generally indicate?
options: a:That summer maintenance is underway.,b:Less-than-ideal driving conditions and that extra caution is needed.,c:That construction will only occur during the day.,d:That you must immediately stop and back up.
note: Orange work zone signs warn that road or utility work is taking place and that normal conditions may be changed. Lanes may narrow, shift, or be closed, workers and equipment may be close to traffic, and surfaces may be rough. You should slow down, be prepared for sudden stops, and use extra caution.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:You must stop before crossing it,b:You may change lanes or pass if it is safe,c:Passing is never allowed,d:Lanes travel in opposite directions
note: A single dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe, after checking mirrors and blind spots and making sure you will not interfere with other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is a correct rule to follow when passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass,b:Pass on the right only when it is legal and safe,c:Try to get to the front of slow traffic by aggressive passing
note: Before passing, signal well in advance—at least 100 feet in most areas, and 200–300 feet when posted for higher speeds—so other drivers know your intentions. Check mirrors and blind spots, make sure you have enough clear space to pass, and return to your lane only when you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down to allow room in front of your vehicle for the other driver to pass,b:Maintain speed and ignore them,c:Brake suddenly to block them,d:Speed up to prevent them
note: If another driver wants to pass you, help them do it safely. Slightly reduce your speed to create more space in front of your vehicle so they have room to move back into the lane. Do not speed up or block them, as that increases the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Slow down and prepare to stop,b:Yield to other cars,c:Go through the intersection quickly
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop before the intersection, unless you are so close that stopping safely is not possible. It is a warning, not a signal to speed up.

question: Which is important to do while driving on major highways?
options: a:Stay alert.,b:Keep your eyes fixed on a single point.,c:Turn off your headlights to save power.
note: On major highways you must stay alert, scan the road ahead, and keep your eyes moving to avoid highway hypnosis. Do not stare at one point, and always use headlights as required by law for visibility and safety.

question: When visibility is reduced by fog, what should you do?
options: a:Use high beams to see farther ahead.,b:Increase speed to quickly clear the fog.,c:Drive cautiously and reduce your speed.
note: In fog, reduce your speed, increase following distance, and drive cautiously. Use low-beam headlights or fog lights so light does not reflect back at you. High beams in fog make it harder to see.

question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane typically mark what?
options: a:That no one has right-of-way in the area.,b:That vehicles have right-of-way over pedestrians.,c:A bike lane only,d:Boundaries of a crosswalk; pedestrians in crosswalks must be given the right-of-way.
note: Two solid white lines across the lane usually mark a crosswalk. Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in the crosswalk and be prepared to stop for people crossing the street.

question: At a crossing marked only with a crossbuck, how should you proceed?
options: a:Speed up across the tracks to minimize time on them.,b:Only proceed when a flagger signals you to go.,c:Assume the crossing is clear and proceed without looking.,d:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when no train is coming.
note: A crossbuck alone means you are at a railroad crossing without active signals. Approach slowly, look and listen for trains in both directions, and cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who goes first?
options: a:The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.,b:The driver to arrive last has the right-of-way.,c:One driver should continue driving without stopping.
note: At a four‑way stop, the first vehicle to come to a complete stop goes first. If two vehicles stop at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Always make full stops and proceed only when it is your turn and the way is clear.

question: After being pulled over, should a driver immediately get out and approach the officer’s squad car?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When an officer pulls you over, stay in your vehicle unless the officer instructs you otherwise. Keep your hands visible, usually on the steering wheel, and follow the officer’s directions. Getting out and approaching the squad car can be unsafe and is generally discouraged.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow changes to a steady green circular light, what must drivers do when turning?
options: a:You may no longer turn under any circumstances.,b:Stop and wait for a green arrow to reappear.,c:You have absolute right-of-way to turn.,d:You may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: When a protected green arrow turns into a steady green circular light, you may still make the turn, but it is no longer protected. You must yield to oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians, and turn only when there is a safe gap.

question: How can you avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spot?
options: a:Quickly glance over your shoulder before changing lanes,b:Adjust rearview mirrors every few minutes,c:Honk before changing lanes,d:Rely solely on side mirrors
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. Use your mirrors and signals, but never rely on mirrors alone to check blind spots.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no signals or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate to cross quickly.,b:Be prepared to yield to any train and cross only when safe.,c:Assume the tracks are inactive.,d:Always stop before crossing the tracks.
note: At a railroad crossing without signals or gates, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely. Never try to beat a train through the crossing.

question: Turning your head to check blind spots before changing lanes is:
options: a:Required only for new drivers.,b:A good driving habit that should be practiced.,c:Unnecessary if you have mirrors.,d:A poor habit because it wastes time.
note: Turning your head to check blind spots before changing lanes is a key part of safe driving. Mirrors do not show everything; there are areas alongside and slightly behind your vehicle that you can only see by briefly glancing over your shoulder. Failing to check blind spots can lead to collisions with vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that you did not see in your mirrors.

question: When making a left turn at an intersection, must you yield to oncoming bicyclists?
options: a:Only if the bicyclist is in a marked bike lane,b:Yes—TRUE,c:Only at night,d:No—FALSE
note: When you turn left, you must yield to all oncoming traffic that is close enough to be a hazard, including bicyclists. Bicycles are vehicles under the law and have the same right-of-way as cars when going straight through an intersection. Treat an oncoming bicycle like an oncoming car: wait until it is safe and clear before completing your left turn.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn them sharply toward the curb.,b:Turn them sharply away from the curb.,c:Point them straight ahead.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will gently touch the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic. On a downhill with a curb, you turn the wheels toward the curb instead.

question: Which statements are true about seat belts and child restraints?
options: a:Airbags make seat belts unnecessary for infants.,b:Children 12 and under should always sit in the front seat.,c:It is safe to place an infant seat in the front seat if it faces forward,d:You should ensure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints and never place a rear-facing infant in a front seat with an active airbag.
note: Seat belts and proper child restraints greatly reduce the risk of injury in a crash. Every passenger should use a seat belt or appropriate child safety seat. Never place a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat if there is an active passenger airbag; the airbag can strike the back of the infant seat with great force and cause serious injury or death.

question: On slick roads, how should you handle turns?
options: a:Turn quickly to maintain momentum,b:Change lanes mid-turn,c:Accelerate through the turn,d:Take turns more slowly than usual
note: On slick or slippery roads, you have less traction, so it is easier to skid when turning. Slow down before the turn and take it more gently than you would on dry pavement. Avoid sudden steering, acceleration, or braking in the turn, as these can cause you to lose control.

question: What does a 'No standing' sign allow you to do?
options: a:Never stop there under any conditions.,b:Park if you remain in the vehicle.,c:Stand outside the vehicle while it is parked,d:Stop temporarily only to pick up or discharge passengers.
note: A 'No standing' sign permits temporary stops to load or unload passengers but not parking.

question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?
options: a:Ignore tire tread condition.,b:Keep cruise control on in rain.,c:Drive faster through puddles,d:Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. The best prevention is to slow down on wet or slushy roads, keep good tire tread and proper inflation, and avoid standing water so your tires can maintain grip.

question: Before changing lanes, which checks should you perform?
options: a:Only signal and change lanes quickly,b:Shout to other drivers then change lanes,c:Only check your rearview mirror,d:Check side and rearview mirrors and glance over your shoulder for blind spots
note: Before changing lanes, check your rearview and side mirrors to see traffic around you, then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you’re moving to check your blind spot. Signal, make sure the lane is clear, and then change lanes smoothly.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, where should you glance?
options: a:Toward the center of the road.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Toward the right side of the road or the right edge line to avoid glare.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, look toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide. This reduces glare and helps you stay in your lane until the vehicle passes. Do not stare into the oncoming headlights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already inside an intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:
options: a:Reverse out of the intersection immediately.,b:Honk and speed up to clear the intersection.,c:Stop in the middle of the intersection.,d:Continue through the intersection carefully.
note: If the light turns yellow after you have entered the intersection, continue through and clear the intersection safely. Do not stop in the middle or try to back up; the yellow is warning that the red is coming, not telling you to stop if you are already inside.

question: Which of these does stopping distance NOT depend on?
options: a:Road surface condition,b:Time of day,c:Your reaction time,d:Condition of vehicle brakes
note: Stopping distance is made up of perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance. These depend on your reaction time, the condition of your brakes and tires, your speed, vehicle weight, and the road surface. The time of day by itself does not directly change how far it takes your vehicle to stop.

question: What is a 'No zone'?
options: a:A designated no-passing area.,b:The blind spot of a large vehicle.,c:A one-way traffic area.
note: A 'No Zone' is the large blind spot around trucks and other large vehicles where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. If you drive in these areas, the truck driver may not know you are there, increasing the risk of a collision. Avoid lingering alongside or close behind large vehicles.

question: If you must drive in fog, should you use high beam headlights?
options: a:Yes, to see farther ahead,b:No, use low beams or fog lights,c:Use parking lights only,d:Turn off all lights
note: In fog, high beams reflect off the water droplets in the air and shine back at you, making it harder to see. Use low beam headlights or fog lights so the light stays on the road surface, and reduce your speed so you have time to react to hazards.

question: What do crossbuck signs warn drivers about?
options: a:Railroad crossings ahead.,b:No passing zones.,c:School zones.,d:Stop signs ahead.
note: A crossbuck sign is the white X-shaped sign at railroad crossings. It marks the location of the tracks and tells drivers to yield to any approaching train, slow down, look and listen, and never try to beat a train through the crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you must yield to traffic when merging and cannot merge safely, does yield also require stopping?
options: a:Only for commercial vehicles.,b:False — yield never requires stopping.,c:True — yield can require stopping if you cannot merge safely.,d:Only during daylight hours.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and be prepared to stop. You may proceed without stopping only if traffic and pedestrians are not close enough to be a hazard. If you cannot safely merge or enter because of other traffic, you must stop and wait until it is safe to go.

question: If another driver cuts you off, the safest response is to:
options: a:Flash high beams and tailgate them.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Pull next to them and argue.,d:Brake-check them immediately.
note: If another driver cuts you off, stay calm and continue driving defensively. Do not retaliate, tailgate, or confront the other driver, because that can quickly escalate into road rage and increase the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs legally indicate?
options: a:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions (and sometimes a posted minimum speed),b:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic,c:Only a suggested speed
note: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions, and in some areas a posted minimum speed. You must never exceed the maximum, and you must slow down below the limit when conditions like rain, fog, traffic, or road work make the posted speed unsafe.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Cut them off to slow them down,b:Retaliate aggressively,c:Avoid eye contact,d:Call them names
note: When you encounter an aggressive driver, avoid eye contact, do not respond to their gestures or actions, and create space between your vehicle and theirs. Let them pass when possible and focus on staying safe rather than engaging with them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Always speed up to beat the light.,b:Make a U-turn immediately.,c:Stop before entering the intersection if it is safe to do so.,d:Ignore it and proceed at the same speed.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, proceed through the intersection with caution.

question: When should you use your turn signals?
options: a:Any time you turn, change lanes, park, or enter or leave traffic.,b:Only when other vehicles are present.,c:Only during daylight hours.,d:Never when turning right.
note: Use your turn signal every time you turn, change lanes, merge, or enter or leave a parking space or roadway. Signaling early and clearly lets other road users know what you plan to do, which helps prevent collisions.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best course of action?
options: a:Lie down in the vehicle and sleep.,b:Stay inside your vehicle and wait for help.,c:Leave the vehicle to seek help immediately.,d:Walk into the road to flag down cars.
note: Staying inside your vehicle in a snowstorm is usually the safest choice. Your car provides shelter from wind and cold, makes you easier for rescuers to find, and reduces the risk of getting lost or struck by other vehicles in low visibility. Run the engine only periodically for heat, keep the exhaust pipe clear of snow, and conserve fuel while you wait for help.

question: Which of the following parking restrictions is illegal in Virginia?
options: a:Parking in a parking lot,b:Parking on private property with permission,c:Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant
note: Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is illegal because it can block or delay firefighters from connecting hoses in an emergency. Even if you stay in the vehicle, you must not stop or park too close to a hydrant. Legal parking includes properly using parking lots and private property when you have the owner’s permission.

question: Guide signs that give directional and mileage information are what color?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Guide or destination signs are green with white lettering. They give directions, route information, and distances to help you navigate to cities, exits, and other destinations. Yellow signs are for warnings, and red signs are for stop, yield, and certain regulatory messages.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:All of the above,b:Condition of brakes and tires,c:Vehicle speed,d:Pavement condition
note: Braking distance increases with higher speed and is affected by how well your brakes and tires work and how good or bad the road surface is. Wet, icy, or gravel roads, worn tires, or poor brakes all lengthen the distance it takes to stop. Because all these factors matter, you must adjust your speed and following distance to conditions.

question: Children under what age must be secured in an approved child safety seat in Virginia?
options: a:Five,b:Six,c:Eight
note: In Virginia, children under age eight must be secured in an approved child safety seat or booster seat. Properly using the correct type of seat for the child’s age, weight, and height greatly reduces the risk of injury in a crash. The requirement applies to most passenger vehicles, with limited exemptions specified in state law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you enter a freeway from an entrance ramp?
options: a:Signal and enter the freeway when safe, yielding to freeway traffic.,b:Signal and enter the freeway; freeway traffic must yield.,c:Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
note: When entering a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to build up speed and match the flow of freeway traffic. Signal your intention to merge, look for a safe gap, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Merge smoothly when it is safe; freeway traffic does not have to yield to you.

question: What does a flashing red light on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Proceed with caution,b:The signal is broken.,c:The same as a stop sign.,d:You do not have to stop.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, look for other vehicles and pedestrians, yield the right‑of‑way as required, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When directed to do so by a flagger or a stop sign or when warning devices are active.,b:Only if a train is visible.,c:You never have to stop.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, flashing lights, or lowered gates indicate a train is coming. Always obey these warnings, look and listen for trains in both directions, and do not proceed until you are sure the tracks are clear and it is safe to cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is the posted maximum speed limit the fastest you are allowed to drive in all conditions?
options: a:True,b:False
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum speed allowed in ideal conditions, not a guaranteed safe speed at all times. You must slow down when roads are wet, icy, or crowded, or when visibility is reduced, so that you can always stop safely within the distance you can see.

question: Why should you avoid following other vehicles too closely?
options: a:You won't see the car's color.,b:You may not have time to stop if they slow or stop suddenly.,c:You may not hear their stereo.,d:It makes lane changes easier
note: If you follow another vehicle too closely, you may not have enough time or space to react if it slows or stops suddenly. Keeping a safe following distance gives you room to brake smoothly, avoid rear‑end collisions, and respond to hazards ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which vehicles are HOV lanes not intended for?
options: a:High-occupancy vehicles.,b:Tractor-trailers.,c:Motorcycles,d:Carpools.
note: High-occupancy vehicle (HOV) lanes are reserved for vehicles carrying multiple people, such as carpools, buses, and often motorcycles and certain clean-fuel vehicles. Large tractor‑trailers are generally not the intended users of HOV lanes because they are not high‑occupancy passenger vehicles and can impede traffic flow in those lanes.

question: What danger can a leaking exhaust system create for vehicle occupants?
options: a:Improved engine performance.,b:Lower fuel efficiency only.,c:Excessive engine oil consumption.,d:Exposure to carbon monoxide that can cause drowsiness or death.
note: A leaking exhaust system can allow exhaust gases, including carbon monoxide, to enter the passenger compartment. Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless and can cause headache, dizziness, drowsiness, and, at high levels or with prolonged exposure, death. Any suspected exhaust leak should be repaired immediately.

question: When should you stop at an accident scene?
options: a:Stop and block the road to prevent others from passing.,b:Stop only to take photos.,c:Only if you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.,d:Always stop and gather a crowd.
note: You should not stop at an accident scene just to look or take photos, because this can create additional hazards and traffic congestion. Stop only if you are directly involved in the crash or if emergency help has not yet arrived and you can safely provide assistance or call 911.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is something you should NOT do when changing lanes?
options: a:Signal to show your intention,b:Fail to check your mirrors and blind spot,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane
note: When changing lanes, you must always check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, and signal before moving. Failing to check mirrors and blind spots is dangerous because another vehicle may be beside you where you cannot see it with a quick forward glance alone.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching, what must you do?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way,b:Stop immediately in your lane to block traffic,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and/or siren approaches, you must yield the right‑of‑way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop if necessary, or otherwise create as clear a path as possible so the emergency vehicle can pass quickly and safely.

question: Which of the following is commonly used to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?
options: a:Flashing red lights.,b:White lines on the road edge.,c:Arrow lane markings.
note: Arrow lane markings painted on the pavement (and sometimes shown on overhead signs) indicate which lanes are for turning left, turning right, or going straight. Drivers should choose their lane based on these arrows well before reaching the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Upon seeing an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Slow down and continue without stopping.,b:Keep driving in your lane.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and/or a siren, you must move as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stop, allowing it a clear path. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs otherwise.

question: Compared to smaller cars, truck and bus blind spots are:
options: a:Much larger,b:About the same size,c:Much smaller
note: Trucks and buses have much larger blind spots than passenger cars, including directly behind, along both sides (especially the right), and sometimes directly in front of the vehicle. Avoid driving for long periods in these areas because the truck or bus driver may not see you.

question: Which has priority over the others at an intersection?
options: a:A steady red light,b:A flashing yellow light,c:A stop sign,d:A police officer directing traffic
note: An authorized police officer or traffic officer directing traffic always has priority over traffic lights, signs, and pavement markings. If their hand signals or directions conflict with a signal or sign, you must follow the officer’s instructions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way intersection where all directions have stop signs and two drivers arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right,b:One driver may continue without stopping,c:The driver on the left
note: At a four-way stop where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Each driver should proceed only after making sure the other driver is yielding and the intersection is clear.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It can lower your ability to focus on driving.,b:It decreases your chances of an accident.,c:It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.,d:It always improves reaction time
note: Emotional stress, anger, or anxiety can distract you from the driving task, slow your reactions, and make you more likely to take risks. If you are very upset, it is safer to delay driving or take time to calm down before you get behind the wheel.

question: Is it illegal for a car to share a single lane with a motorcycle?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane, and a car must not crowd or ride side‑by‑side with a motorcycle in the same lane. However, it is not generally illegal for a car and a motorcycle to be in the same lane during a normal passing maneuver; the car may legally change lanes or pass when safe and allowed by markings. What is prohibited is lane sharing or straddling the lane alongside the motorcycle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a two-lane road marked with a broken yellow centerline, what does that tell you?
options: a:It is a one-way road.,b:The road is closed for repairs.,c:You must stop before entering.,d:Traffic on that road moves in both directions (two-way road).
note: A yellow centerline always separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the yellow line is broken, it means you are on a two‑way road and passing is allowed when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited by signs or conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The driver on your left, because they were there first,b:You have the right of way — the driver to your left must yield to you,c:Whoever signals first proceeds first,d:The driver going straight always has priority
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. Since the other driver is to your LEFT, you are to their right — meaning you have the right of way and should proceed first.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,b:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
note: If you must stop on an interstate, pull completely off the travel lanes onto the shoulder if possible, turn on your emergency flashers so others can see you, and stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt fastened unless there is an immediate danger such as fire or traffic striking your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass on a two-lane road, what should be your primary check?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Sound your horn as you pass.,d:Assume oncoming traffic will slow down.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, your main concern is whether there is enough clear space ahead in the oncoming lane. Carefully judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles and only begin passing if you are sure you can complete the maneuver and return to your lane without forcing any other driver to slow or swerve.

question: On which road marking may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,b:You are on a hill or curve.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken center line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe. A solid line next to your lane means you must not pass, and you should never pass on hills, curves, or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is limited.
